It makes the classmate feel less alone. Because it shows the classmate that someone has noticed and cares, the sadness is easier to bear.
Why do people lower their voices when a baby is asleep in the room?
A baby wakes easily. Because loud sounds can wake a sleeping baby, quiet voices let the baby and tired parents rest.
Why do people often feel cheerful on the morning of a holiday?
The day ahead is free and enjoyable. Because there is no rush to get anywhere and people have enjoyable things to look forward to, their minds feel light.
Why do two magnets sometimes push each other away?

Magnets push apart when the same ends face each other. Because each magnet has a north and a south end, and matching ends repel while different ends attract, turning one round changes the push into a pull.
Why does an iron gate rust but a gold ring does not?
Iron is easily changed by the weather and gold is not. Because iron slowly reacts with water and air to make rust, while gold hardly reacts with anything, the ring stays shiny.
Why do owls come out at night?
Night is when their food is out. Because they hunt small animals that move around after dark, and their large eyes and sharp hearing suit the dark, they find food easily.
Why do spider webs sparkle on a misty morning?
Mist leaves water drops on the web. Because tiny drops of water cling to the thin threads and each drop catches the light, the web glitters.
Why do some friends slowly drift apart?
They stop sharing time and interests. Because they spend less time together and their interests change, they have fewer things to share and the bond weakens.
Why does tea cool faster in a wide saucer than in a cup?
More of the tea touches the air. Because a wide, shallow layer has more surface open to the air, more heat escapes and more water dries off.
Why does a pet dog rush to the door when its owner comes home?
It is glad to see its owner. Because it has bonded with its owner, it expects attention, and it may also hope for a walk or a treat.
Why does bread turn brown in a toaster?
Strong heat changes the sugars and proteins on its surface. Because these react together, they make a brown colour and a new, toasty flavour.
Why does our stomach rumble when we have not eaten for a while?
The gut keeps moving even when it is empty. Because its muscles squeeze air and liquid along, and no food is there to muffle the sound, we hear the noise.
Why do cactus plants have spines instead of ordinary leaves?
Spines save water. Because they lose far less water than broad leaves and also keep thirsty animals from eating the plant, the cactus can live in dry places.
Why do people say please when they ask for something?
Please shows respect. Because it leaves the other person free to say yes, people are usually happier to help.
All roses are flowers, and all flowers need water. Do roses need water?
Yes, roses need water. Because roses are flowers and every flower needs water, the rule that covers all flowers covers roses too.
Why might a person laugh along with others who are teasing him even though it hurts?
Laughing may feel like the safest choice. Because laughing can hide hurt feelings, help him fit in and avoid even more teasing, it seems the least risky reaction at that moment.
Why does a group project go badly when one person does all the work?
The work is unevenly shared. Because that person gets tired and annoyed while the others learn nothing and feel they do not belong, the team stops working as a team.
Why do children take turns on a playground slide?
Everyone gets a chance. Because nobody has to push, there are fewer quarrels and fewer chances of someone being knocked over.
Why do shadows nearly vanish on a cloudy day?
Clouds soften the sunlight. Because clouds scatter the sunlight so it reaches us from every part of the sky, there is no bright spot to make a sharp dark patch.
Why does a see-saw tip down on the heavier child's side?
Gravity pulls harder on the heavier child. Because the heavier child pulls the board down harder than the lighter child can pull the other side, the heavier end goes down.
Why does fog gather near a river on a cold morning?
The air above the water cools. Because cool air cannot hold as much water vapour, the extra vapour turns into tiny floating droplets that we see as fog.
Why should seeds be sown before the rainy season rather than after it ends?
Seeds sown before the rains get water when they need it. Because the rain provides the water the seeds need to sprout and the plants to grow, they get a good start without extra watering.
Is it wrong to accept food from a stranger?
Yes, it is unsafe to accept it. Because you cannot be sure who prepared it or why it is being offered, a safe choice is to say no thank you and tell a trusted adult.
Why do small sounds seem louder at night?
Everything else is quieter. Because there is less traffic and chatter, small noises are not covered up and stand out clearly.
Our neighbour's dog barks only at strangers. It barked at me yesterday. Am I a stranger to it?
Yes, I am a stranger to it. Because the dog barks only at strangers and it barked at me, the dog must see me as one.
What is sleep for?
Sleep lets the body and brain rest and recover. Because the body repairs itself and the brain sorts out what we learned during the day while we sleep, we feel clearer and stronger afterwards.
Why do roads in the hills wind in zigzags?
The roads zigzag to make the climb gentle. Because a straight road up a steep hill would be too steep for vehicles to climb safely, a winding path spreads the slope over a longer distance.
Why does a cut potato stay pale if we keep it in a bowl of water?
Water keeps air away from the cut surface. Because the dark colour comes from the cut surface reacting with air, covering it with water slows that change.
Why does a glass of water on a sunny windowsill sometimes throw a tiny rainbow on the wall?
The glass bends and splits sunlight. Because each colour in white light bends by a slightly different amount, the colours spread apart and land in separate stripes on the wall.
Why does our own voice sound different when we hear it on a recording?
We hear our own voice partly through our head. Because the sound also travels through bone, it seems deeper to us, while a recording carries only the part that went through the air.
Why is it unsafe to swim in a river after heavy rain?
The river becomes fast and unpredictable. Because rain adds a lot of water and makes the current strong and hides rocks and branches under the muddy surface, even good swimmers can be swept away.
Why do people often wear new clothes on a festival day?
It is a way of dressing up for the celebration. Because people like to mark an occasion with something fresh and good, wearing them adds to the feeling of celebration.
Why does paint peel off a wall that is damp?
Water gets behind the paint. Because moisture pushes up from inside the wall and loosens the grip of the paint, the paint lifts in flakes.
Why do we feel bored in a long waiting room?
The mind has nothing interesting to hold its attention. Because attention keeps drifting to the passing time when nothing engages it, the minutes seem to crawl.
Why does it hurt when a friend forgets our name?
A name is part of who we are. Because remembering it tells us someone paid attention to us, forgetting it makes us feel unnoticed.
Why do bees keep visiting flowers?
Bees eat the sweet nectar. Because they brush against pollen while feeding and carry it from flower to flower, the plants can make seeds as a result.
If I leave a blown-up balloon on a sunny windowsill, why might it burst?
The air inside gets hotter. Because warm air spreads out and pushes harder on the rubber, the thin skin is stretched past what it can take.
Why does water roll off a duck's back instead of soaking in?
The feathers are oily. Because the oil makes the feathers repel water, the duck's body stays dry and warm even when it swims.
Does splitting a big project into small parts make it easier to finish, and why?
Yes, it does. Because a huge task can seem too heavy to begin and small steps show quick progress, we keep going.
Why is it helpful to write the date at the top of each notebook page?
The date helps us find things later. Because notes are written over many days, the dates show the order of the lessons and make it easier to find a topic when we revise.
If the door is locked, the hall light stays off. Today the hall light is off. Is the door locked?
We cannot be sure. Because the rule only tells us what happens when the door is locked, the light could be off for another reason, such as a switch or a fault.
Why do children ask so many why questions?
The world is new to them. Because they are curious and want to understand how things work, asking is the quickest way to learn.
Why don't clouds fall down although they are made of water?
Their drops are tiny and light. Because the droplets are so small that rising air keeps carrying them upwards, they drift instead of dropping, until they join into drops big enough to fall as rain.
What makes pushing a trolley up a ramp easier than lifting it straight up?
A ramp makes the climb gentle. Because the trolley goes up a long slope instead of a sudden steep climb, the push needed at any moment is smaller.
In a dusty room, why can we see the beam of a torch?
Dust scatters some of the light. Because tiny specks send light in every direction, a little of it reaches our eyes from the side, and the path becomes visible.
Why do footballers wear boots with studs on the soles?
The studs give extra grip. Because they dig into the grass and stop the foot from sliding, a player can run and turn quickly without slipping.
Why does our face turn red after we run?
More blood flows near the skin. Because running makes the body hot, the small blood vessels in the skin widen to let the heat escape into the air.
Why do families cook special dishes at festivals?
Special dishes mark the day as different from others. Because food made with extra care and shared with family feels like a treat, it makes the festival memorable.
Why do we get shy when many people are looking at us?
We worry about being judged. Because attention makes us notice every small thing we say or do, we become self-conscious and stop feeling at ease.
Why can a dog respond to a whistle that people cannot hear?
Dog ears pick up higher sounds than ours. Because human hearing stops at a lower pitch, a very high whistle sounds like nothing to us but is clear to the dog.
All the pencils in this box are blue. Gita took one out of the box. What colour is her pencil?
Her pencil is blue. Because every pencil in the box is blue and hers came from that box, it must be blue.
Why do farmers plough a field before sowing seeds?
Farmers plough to loosen the soil. Because loose soil lets roots spread and lets air and water reach them, and ploughing also buries weeds, young plants grow better.
Why should we leave a little spare time between two tasks in our day?
A gap soaks up delays. Because tasks often take longer than we expect, a gap stops a delay from spoiling everything that comes next.
Why does a pot lid sometimes stay stuck to the pot after the food inside has cooled?
The air outside presses the lid down. Because the steam inside turned back into water as the pot cooled and left less pressure inside, the outside air presses the lid tight.
How does glue hold two pieces of paper together?
Glue sticks to the paper and sets hard. Because it flows into the tiny gaps between the paper fibres before it dries, it locks the sheets together.
Why does a ceiling fan keep turning for a while after we switch it off?

Inertia, the tendency of a moving thing to keep moving, keeps it turning. Because the heavy blades carry a lot of motion and only friction in the bearings and air resistance slow them, they take a while to stop.
Why do some people find it hard to say no to their friends?
They fear upsetting the friend. Because people want to be liked and often worry that a refusal will end the friendship, they say yes even when they would rather not.
Why should we fly a kite far away from electric wires?
Wires can give a dangerous shock. Because a string or kite caught on a wire can carry electricity, especially if it is damp, the person holding it could be badly hurt.
Why do we learn a puzzle better by trying it ourselves than by only watching someone solve it?
Doing it fixes the steps in memory better. Because the mind learns most when it has to think and make mistakes, active solving beats watching.
Why does a little sister want to join in all her elder brother's games?
She looks up to him. Because children enjoy doing what the people they admire do, being part of his game makes her feel grown up.
Why is the sand at the beach burning hot at noon while the sea water feels cool?
The sand warms up much faster than water. Because water needs a lot more heat to change its temperature and also mixes the warmth into deeper water, the sea stays cool.
Why does a caterpillar eat leaves almost all day?
It must grow. Because it will later change into a butterfly or moth and cannot feed much during the change, it stores up food while it can.
Thick card is easier to cut with scissors near the hinge. Why?
The blades squeeze the card harder near the pivot. Because the blades act like a lever, the same push at the handles gives a bigger squeeze on the card the closer it is to the pivot.
Why do people arrive at the railway station well before the train leaves?
Trains do not wait. Because there may be a queue, a platform to find or a delay on the way, extra time keeps them from missing the train.
Why do players warm up before a match?
Their muscles get ready. Because gentle exercise loosens the muscles and sends more blood to them, they move better and are less likely to be strained.
Why do we cough when a crumb goes down the wrong way?
The body is trying to clear the airway. Because a crumb in the windpipe blocks air and sets off a reflex, a strong push of air is sent out to throw it back up.
Why do soap bubbles show swirling colours?
Light reflects from both sides of their thin skin. Because the reflections from the front and the back of the soapy film mix, some colours grow stronger while others fade.
Why does a bush grow bushier when the gardener snips its tips?
Side buds start to grow. Because the tip of a shoot holds back the buds below it, cutting it off lets them grow into new branches.
Anyone with a ticket may enter the hall. Nina walked in. Must she have a ticket?
We cannot be sure. Because the rule says people with tickets may enter but does not say that nobody else may, Nina may have been let in for some other reason.
Why do picnic organisers write a list of who brings what?
A list prevents mistakes. Because without it several people might bring the same dish while nobody brings plates, and with it every need is covered once.
Why does a train horn sound higher as the train comes nearer and lower once it has passed?

The train's movement changes the sound waves. Because the sound waves are squeezed together as the train comes towards us and stretched apart as it goes away, our ears hear a higher note and then a lower one.
Why do small lamps look so bright on a dark evening?
Everything around them is dark. Because our eyes judge brightness by comparison and adjust to the dim surroundings, even a tiny flame stands out.
A friend is upset with me. What is a sensible first step?

A good first step is to talk to the friend calmly and listen. Because anger usually fades when a person feels understood, hearing their side gives us a chance to say sorry if we were wrong and fix things.
Why is a family meal a good time to talk?
Everyone sits together without hurry. Because there are no other tasks pulling attention away, people can tell each other about their day.
Why does ironing smooth out the creases in a shirt?
Heat and pressing flatten the fibres. Because warm fibres become soft and can be flattened, and they stay that way as they cool, the creases disappear.
Is revising a lesson on the day it was taught really better? Why?
Yes, it helps us remember. Because new facts fade from memory unless they are used again, a quick look soon afterwards helps them stay.
Why should a toaster be unplugged before we clean it?
It should be unplugged to prevent an electric shock. Because the heating parts inside are connected to the mains, cleaning around them while the power is on could give a dangerous jolt.
Why does a cool breeze blow from the sea towards the land in the afternoon?
The land has become warmer than the sea. Because warm air above the land rises and cooler air from the sea moves in to fill the space, we feel a breeze from the water.
Why does a cat usually land on its feet when it falls?
Its body twists in the air. Because cats have very flexible spines and a quick sense of balance, they turn their bodies the right way up before they reach the ground.
Why does food cook faster in a pressure cooker?
The water inside gets hotter than usual. Because the closed lid traps steam and raises the pressure, the water boils at a higher temperature and softens the food sooner.
Why is the door handle fixed far from the hinge?
The handle is far from the hinge so the door is easy to push. Because force applied far from the pivot turns the door more easily, a light push is enough.
Why are there speed bumps on the road near a school?
Speed bumps make drivers slow down. Because a fast car jolts badly over a bump, drivers ease off, and children crossing the road are much safer from slow traffic.
What makes some people short-tempered when they are hungry?
The body lacks fuel. Because tired, hungry people have less patience and self-control, small annoyances seem much bigger.
My wooden cupboard door sticks in the monsoon but opens easily in winter. What is going on?
The wood has swollen a little. Because wood soaks up water from the damp monsoon air, it expands and rubs against the frame, and it shrinks again when the air dries.
Why do runners stay in their own lanes on a track?
Runners stay in their lanes to keep the race fair. Because jostling or cutting across would slow other runners and give some an unfair gain, lanes give each person a clear path.
Why do people have two eyes and not just one?
Eyes working as a pair help us judge how far away things are. Because each eye sees from a slightly different spot, the brain compares the pictures and works out depth.
Why do road signs glow in the headlights of a car at night, though they have no bulbs?
Their coating returns the light. Because the coating sends the headlight beam straight back towards the car, the driver sees a bright sign.
Lena says the film must be good because the audience clapped at the end. Is she certain about that?
No, she cannot be certain. Because people may clap to be polite or because they are glad it is over, clapping alone does not prove that the film was good.
Why do people check the weather report before planning a picnic?
They check the report so the picnic is not ruined. Because rain or strong heat would make the day unpleasant, knowing in advance lets them pick a better day.
Why do the leaves of a plant droop when the soil gets very dry?
The leaves lose their firmness. Because plant cells stay stiff when they are full of water, a plant with too little water in its soil goes limp.
Why might a classmate not want to talk about a bad exam result?
The classmate may feel embarrassed. Because a poor result can seem like a sign of failure, talking about it brings the unpleasant feeling back, so they would rather keep quiet.
Why do we keep a doormat outside the front door?
The mat catches dirt. Because shoes carry mud and dust and rubbing them on the mat removes much of it, less dirt gets carried onto the floor inside.
Why do people share sweets with their neighbours during festivals?
It strengthens neighbourly bonds. Because giving something nice shows that we care about those who live near us, it builds friendship and good feeling in the lane.
Why do families keep old photographs?
They keep memories safe. Because a picture can bring back a person, a place or a day that has slipped from memory, it keeps those times close.
Why does a pulley make it easier to lift a bucket from a well?
A pulley makes lifting easier by changing the direction of the pull. Because you pull down on the rope and can use your own weight, it is more comfortable than lifting the bucket straight up.
Why does a quiet corner help a student prepare for exams?
There is less to distract the mind. Because attention is easily pulled away by noise and movement, a calm place lets us stay with the work for longer.
Why does a hot pan spit and hiss when a few drops of water fall into the oil?
The water turns to steam at once. Because water is heavier than oil and sinks to the bottom of the hot pan, it boils violently there and throws the oil upwards.
Why should children never play near an open well?
A fall could be very dangerous. Because an open well is deep and the sides are hard to climb out of, a child who falls in might not get out alone.
Why do frogs start croaking loudly after the first rains?
It is their time to find mates. Because ponds and puddles fill up with water where eggs can be laid, the male frogs call to attract females.
Why does wet mud turn hard and crack under the hot sun?
The water in the mud dries away. Because the tiny clay grains stick tightly together as the water leaves and the mud shrinks, the ground splits into cracks.
Why does a small boat rock when a big boat passes by?
The passing boat makes waves. Because the big boat pushes water aside as it moves and makes ripples that spread out and reach the small boat, it is lifted and dropped as they pass.
Why does music from a closed room sound dull and boomy from outside?
The wall lets low notes through more easily. Because walls stop the sharp, high sounds better than the deep ones, mostly the thumping bass reaches us.
Why does a nail left near the sea rust faster than one kept far inland?
Salt in the air speeds up rusting. Because salt dissolves in the thin film of damp on the metal and helps the rusting change happen more quickly, the iron wears away sooner.
Why can one small act of kindness cheer us up on a bad day?
It shows someone cares. Because feeling cared for makes problems seem easier to carry, the day looks less bleak.
Why can we see a glowing lamp from far away at night but not an unlit one?
A glowing lamp makes its own light. Because an unlit object is seen only when other light bounces off it into our eyes and the night has so little of that, it disappears into the dark.
Nobody in the school choir is late today. Hari is in the choir. Is Hari late?
No, Hari is not late. Because no member of the choir is late and Hari is a member, he must be on time.
Why do we squint when we step into bright sunshine?
Squinting lets in less light. Because narrowing the eyelids cuts down the amount of light reaching the eye, the glare hurts less and we can see better.
Why do heavy curtains help to keep a room cooler in the afternoon?
They keep the sun out. Because sunlight coming through a window turns into heat inside a room, blocking it before it enters leaves the room cooler.
Why is it good to listen to a friend's problem without interrupting?
It shows we care. Because people want to feel heard before they want advice, letting them finish tells them we take their worry seriously.
What are the lines we see on a leaf for?
The lines are tiny pipes called veins. Because they carry water to every part of the leaf and carry the food the leaf makes away to the rest of the plant, the leaf can stay alive and flat.
Why do players from opposing teams shake hands after a match?
They shake hands to show good sportsmanship. Because the game was a contest and not a quarrel, the handshake tells everyone that they respect each other whatever the result.
Why do kites fly best on a windy day?
Wind gives the kite its lift. Because moving air pushes against the tilted kite and lifts it, a calm day leaves the kite hanging limply.
Why do screws usually hold wood better than nails?
Their threads grip the wood. Because the spiral ridges bite into the wood and must be turned back out and not simply pulled, they resist being pulled free.
Why should a child tell an adult at once when they see smoke in the house?
Smoke may mean a fire. Because a small fire can spread fast and an adult knows how to get everyone out safely, quick news saves time.
Why does cooked rice stick together in a lump?
Sticky starch glues the grains. Because the grains give out starch as they cook in water, it acts like a glue between them when they cool.
Why does the same rule apply to every child in a school?
The same rule applies to everyone to keep things fair. Because children would feel cheated if some of them could do what others were not allowed to do, equal rules build trust.
Why is a clear night usually colder than a cloudy night?
Clouds keep warmth near the ground. Because clouds act like a blanket, the ground stays warmer on a cloudy night, while on a clear night the heat escapes straight into the sky.
Why does a tin-can telephone only work when the string is pulled tight?
The sound travels along the string as a shaking. Because a loose string sags and soaks up the shakes instead of passing them on, the voice fades before it reaches the other can.
Why do parents repeat the same reminders many times?
Children often forget. Because children are often busy with other things, a gentle repeat helps them remember.
Friends are coming to lunch tomorrow. Should I tidy the house tonight or leave it for the last moment?
Tidy most of it tonight. Because a rushed clean-up in the morning leaves no time for cooking and a last-minute problem, and tonight's work lets you stay calm when the guests arrive.
Why does an aeroplane need a very long runway?
The plane has to reach a high speed. Because a plane lifts off only when it moves fast enough for the air under its wings to hold it, it needs plenty of ground to build up that speed.
Why do small fish swim together in large groups?
Fish swim in groups for safety. Because a predator finds it hard to pick out one fish from a moving crowd, and many eyes notice danger sooner, each fish is less likely to be caught.
Why does a sheet of paper tear so easily after it gets soaked in water?
Wet paper loses much of its strength. Because water gets in between the fibres and loosens the bonds that hold them together, they slide apart with only a small pull.
After telling a lie to a friend, why do we feel bad?
We know we have been unfair to them. Because lying breaks trust, and most people care about being honest with those they like, the guilt stays with us.
Why do sunglasses make a bright afternoon easier on the eyes?
Sunglasses cut down the glare and dim the light reaching the eyes. Because the dark lenses block part of the light before it enters the eye, the eyes do not have to squint so much.
Why do our legs feel heavy after climbing many stairs?
The leg muscles are worn out from lifting the body up each step. Because working muscles use up their fuel and gather tiring waste in them, they cannot pull as strongly until they have rested.
The red box is heavier than the green box, and the blue box is lighter than the green box. Which box is the heaviest?
The red box is the heaviest. Because the red box is heavier than the green one and the green one is heavier than the blue one, red is above the others.
Why does a vegetable patch grow badly when weeds are left to take over?
Weeds take over the soil and leave the vegetables short of what they need. Because weeds use up water, light and nutrients in the soil, there is less left for the plants we want.
Why does a rolling ball slow down and stop on a grass field?
The ball loses its speed to rubbing against the grass. Because this rubbing, called friction, works against the motion and takes away its energy, the ball comes to rest.
Why do schools hold rehearsals before the annual function?
Rehearsals help the function to go smoothly. Because every child learns when to come on and what to do, and mistakes can be fixed in advance, the real show has fewer surprises.
Why should matches be kept out of the reach of small children?

Matches are kept out of reach so that a small child cannot light one by mistake. Because small children are curious and do not understand that a flame can cause burns or a fire, they may strike a match just to see what happens.
Why do clothes smell damp when they dry indoors during the monsoon?
Slow drying leaves the clothes wet for a long time and gives them a musty smell. Because the humid air takes away water slowly, tiny germs can grow in the damp cloth and make that smell.
Why does dosa batter rise and bubble when left overnight?
Tiny living yeast and bacteria in the batter make it puff up. Because they feed on the sugars in the batter and give off gas, the gas fills it with bubbles.
How does a car stay on the road when it goes round a bend?
The grip between the tyres and the road keeps the car on its curved path. Because this friction pulls the car towards the inside of the curve instead of letting it slide straight on, the car turns.
Why does a school have a bell?
The bell tells everyone the same thing at the same time. Because a loud, clear sound can be heard in every corner of the building, students and teachers know when to begin and finish the lessons.
Why is it a good idea to leave a spare key with a trusted neighbour?
A spare key gives us a way back into the house if we are locked out. Because a trusted neighbour can open the door if we lose our own key or lock ourselves out, we are not stranded.
Why is it colder at the top of a mountain than in the valley below?
The air is thinner and cooler high on a mountain. Because thin air holds less heat, and the warm ground that heats the air in the valley is far below, the mountain top stays chilly.
Is it fair to judge a classmate by one bad day?
No, it is not fair. Because one bad day shows only a small part of a person and anyone can be tired or upset, we need to see how they usually behave before we decide.
Why can we hear a person talking in the next room even though we cannot see them?

Sound can bend around corners and pass through thin walls, but light cannot. Because sound slips through gaps and shakes thin walls, while light travels straight and is blocked by the wall, we hear without seeing.
Why do tyres have grooves cut into the rubber?
The grooves help the tyre grip the road. Because they give water somewhere to go as the tyre rolls and give the rubber little edges to bite, the tyre does not skid as easily in the wet.
Why are people so curious about a closed gift box?
A closed box hides something we want to know. Because the mind likes to fill in missing knowledge and the box hides the answer, the wish to find out grows stronger.
Why does a baby smile at familiar faces more than at strangers?
Familiar faces make a baby feel safe and happy. Because babies learn quickly who cares for them and relax in their company, they show happiness to those people.
Why do elephants spray mud or dust on their backs?
Elephants cover themselves to protect their skin. Because a coat of mud keeps off the sun and cools the skin, and it keeps biting insects away, the elephant stays comfortable.
Why do railway tracks have tiny gaps between their sections?
The gaps leave room for the steel to grow. Because metal expands when the sun heats it, joined rails with no gaps would push against each other and bend out of shape.
Why do tall buildings appear upside down in a still puddle?

Still water acts like a mirror and flips the picture, so the top of the building is at the bottom. Because light from the top of the building travels down to the surface and bounces up to our eyes at a slant, the top appears at the lowest part of the picture.
Why can't a person tickle themselves?

Our own touch cannot surprise us, so it does not feel ticklish. Because the brain knows what the hand will do before it does it and so treats the feeling as harmless, the surprise that makes tickling funny is missing.
Mira, Raju and Sam sit in a row. Mira is to the left of Raju, and Raju is to the left of Sam. Who sits in the middle?
Raju sits in the middle. Because Mira is to his left and Sam is to his right, he is between them.
Why does a cut flower last longer when it is kept in a vase of water?
Water in the vase keeps the stem supplied, so the flower stays fresh. Because water travels up thin tubes inside the stem to the petals and leaves, the flower does not dry out.
Why should children keep away from a building site?
Building sites are dangerous. Because there are heavy objects, open holes and moving machines and workers cannot always see small children, a child might easily be hurt.
Why are roads slippery in the first few minutes of a rain shower?
Rain mixes with the dust and oil on the road and makes a slippery film. Because this thin muddy film sits between the tyres and the road, the grip is poor until more rain washes it away.
Why do we have day and night?
The side of the Earth facing the sun has day while the other side has night. Because the Earth turns all the way round every day, each place is carried into the light and then away from it.
Why does a firecracker make such a sudden loud bang?
The bang comes from a quick burst of gas. Because the burning powder makes a lot of hot gas in a flash and the gas shoves the air outward sharply, we hear a loud crack.
How does a mosquito net protect a sleeping person?
The net protects by keeping mosquitoes away. Because its tiny holes are too small for the insects to pass through, they cannot reach the skin to bite.
Why does a big drum sound deeper than a small one?
The big drum's skin shakes more slowly, which gives a lower note. Because a larger, heavier skin takes longer to move back and forth than a small, tight skin, it makes fewer shakes in the same time.
Why do students feel proud when their drawing is put up on the classroom wall?
A display shows the students that their work is valued. Because people like to see that their effort matters to others, being put on the wall tells them that what they made is worth showing.
Why do high jumpers land on thick soft mats?
They land on mats to avoid injury. Because a soft mat slows the jumper gently over a longer time than hard ground would, the force on the body is much smaller.
Why do friends often grow closer after finishing a hard task together?
Sharing a hard task makes friends feel more connected. Because working through difficulty side by side builds trust, and each person sees the others being helpful, the bond becomes stronger.
Why is it sensible to plan the route before a long cycle ride with friends?
A planned route keeps the group together and on track. Because everyone then knows where to go and where to stop for rest, nobody gets lost or left behind.
Why do we soak dried chickpeas before cooking them?
We soak chickpeas to make them cook quicker. Because the hard dry seeds take in water and swell, they are already part-softened before they go on the stove.
How can we feel lonely in a crowded place?
Loneliness depends on connection, not on how many people are near. Because being surrounded by strangers does not give us anyone who knows or cares about us, we feel apart.
Why does a torch fail to light if one battery is put in the wrong way round?

A reversed battery breaks the flow of electricity, so the bulb stays dark. Because the batteries must be placed so that their positive and negative ends line up in the circuit, a reversed battery blocks the flow.
Why do parents ask us to tell them once we reach a friend's house?
A short message tells parents that we have arrived safely. Because it ends their worry at once, it is a small way to give them peace.
Why does a dog sniff everything on its walk?
A dog sniffs to learn about the world around it. Because smell is its main sense and its nose is far more sensitive than ours, each sniff tells it who has passed that way and what food is nearby.
Why does a ceramic cup shatter on a stone floor while a steel cup only gets a dent?
The ceramic cup cannot bend, so it breaks, while steel can give a little. Because steel bends a little under a knock and absorbs the force, it dents instead of breaking.
A thin curtain lets in daylight but a thick one makes the room dark. Why is that?

Thick curtains block much more light than thin ones. Because closely woven heavy cloth blocks most of the light, while thin cloth has tiny gaps and passes some through, the thin curtain only dims the room.
Why do we feel no pain when we trim the ends of our fingernails?
The hard tip of the nail has no feeling, so trimming does not hurt. Because the nerves lie in the skin underneath and not in the hard nail itself, the cut ends are like dry hair.
Why should we walk slowly on a freshly mopped floor?
A freshly mopped floor is slippery, so slow steps are safer. Because a thin layer of water cuts down the grip between shoes and the floor, a quick step can slide away and cause a fall.
Why do people decorate their doorways with flowers and rangoli during festivals?
They decorate to welcome visitors and show joy. Because a bright, pretty entrance tells guests they are expected and the family has taken trouble for them, the house feels festive.
Why do teachers give homework?
Homework gives students practice. Because skills grow stronger when we use them again and again, working at home helps a lesson settle in the mind.
Why do some seeds have little wings or soft fluff?
Wings and fluff help seeds travel. Because the wind can carry such light parts a long way, the seeds land away from the parent plant and have room to grow.
Why do rivers always flow downhill?
Rivers run to the lowest ground they can reach, which leads to the sea. Because gravity pulls water down, and water is free to move over ground that slopes towards the sea, it keeps running downhill.
Why does a friend feel hurt when we cancel our plans at the last minute?
A last-minute cancellation can make the friend feel unimportant. Because they may have saved time for us and looked forward to the meeting, a sudden change feels like their time was not valued.
Why do fresh green leaves turn limp when left on a hot kitchen counter?
Warm air dries the leaves out, and they lose their crispness. Because plant cells are firm only when full of water, leaves that lose water go limp.
Either the cat or the dog ate the biscuit, not both. The dog was out of the house when it vanished. Who ate it?
The cat ate it. Because it was the cat or the dog and the dog was not in the house, the dog could not have eaten it.
How can the taps in a house get water from a tank on the roof without a pump?
Gravity pushes the water down from the roof tank through the pipes. Because the tank is higher than the taps and water always runs towards lower places, it flows out of the taps without a pump.
Why does a flute give a higher note when more of its holes are left open?
Opening more holes makes the shaking column of air shorter, and the note higher. Because a short column of air shakes faster than a long one, the pitch we hear goes up.
Why do bus drivers slow down at sharp turns?

A bus driver slows down to keep the bus steady through a sharp turn. Because a moving vehicle wants to keep going straight and the tyres can only grip so much, a sharp turn at speed could make it skid or tip.
Why do goalkeepers wear gloves?
Goalkeepers wear gloves for grip and protection. Because the rough surface of the glove helps hold a slippery ball and the padding softens the hit, saves are easier and less painful.
Our class cannot agree on where to go for the annual trip because everyone wants a different place. How should we decide?
The class should hold a vote. Because every student gets a say and the result is clear, most people will accept it as fair even if their own choice does not win.
Why do bicycles have gears?
Gears help the rider cope with different ground. Because a low gear makes the pedals easy to push uphill and a high gear gives more speed on flat roads, the rider can save effort.
Why do deer and rabbits have eyes on the sides of their heads?
Their eyes sit on the sides so they can see almost all around. Because these animals are hunted, spotting danger coming from any direction gives them time to run.
A candle melts over a small flame, but a steel bowl does not. Why?
Wax melts at a low temperature, but steel needs far more heat. Because an ordinary flame is hot enough to turn wax liquid yet far below the temperature steel needs, the bowl only gets hot.
Why do cousins who meet only on holidays often feel close?

Cousins stay close through shared family stories and fun times together. Because they play together in a relaxed way and belong to the same family, they feel at ease with each other even after long gaps.
Why does a sad song sometimes make a sad person feel a little better?
A sad song can make sadness feel lighter and easier to share. Because feeling understood is a comfort, hearing that someone else has felt the same way helps the sadness ease.
How do spectacles help a person see clearly?
Spectacles bend light so that the picture comes into focus. Because the curved glass bends the light before it enters the eye, the picture lands sharply at the back of the eye instead of blurred.
Why is it better to water the garden in the evening than at noon?
Evening watering wastes less water than watering at noon. Because the sun is weaker and the air is cooler, less of the water dries into the air and more soaks down to the roots.
Why does butter melt so fast on a hot paratha?
Butter melts fast at only a little warmth. Because the fat in butter turns liquid at a low temperature, the heat from the paratha softens it within seconds.
Why do new friends ask each other so many questions?
They ask many questions to get to know one another. Because they have not yet shared any history, questions are the quickest way to find what they like and what they have in common.
Some of the books on the shelf are new. Can we say that every book on the shelf is new?
No, we cannot say that. Because the word some tells us only that at least a part of them are new, it says nothing about the rest, which may be old or new.
Why does water in a clay pot stay cooler than in a steel bottle on a hot day?
The clay lets a little water seep to the outside, which cools the pot. Because that water dries off the surface and drying takes heat away from the pot, the water inside gets colder.
Why do people carry a water bottle on a long road trip?

A bottle gives travellers a drink whenever they need it on the road. Because the journey can be long, there may be no shop for a long stretch, and the body needs drink when it is hot, a bottle saves them from thirst.
Why do we check the brakes of a bicycle before riding down a long slope?
Good brakes are needed on a slope to keep the speed under control. Because gravity pulls the bicycle faster and faster downhill, a rider with poor brakes cannot slow down or stop in time.
Why do swimmers often wear a cap?
A cap helps a swimmer move faster. Because loose hair drags in the water and slows the swimmer down, covering it keeps the head smooth.
Why are chairs usually kept ready for the elders at a festival gathering?
Chairs are kept for elders out of respect and comfort. Because older people tire sooner when standing for long, a seat lets them enjoy the event.
Why is it easier to loosen a tight nut with a long spanner than a short one?
A long spanner turns the nut with less push. Because a longer handle gives the hand more leverage, a small push at the end turns the nut with a bigger twist.
Why does a ringing bell go silent the moment you touch it with your hand?
Touching the bell stops its shaking, so the sound ends at once. Because sound is made by the metal vibrating, and your hand holds the metal still, nothing is left to push the air.
The morning will be sunny and the afternoon rainy, and I have a heavy blanket to dry outside. When should I hang it out?
Hang it out first thing in the morning. Because a heavy blanket needs the longest stretch of sun to dry, and starting early lets it dry fully before the rain arrives.
Why does a snake keep flicking its tongue in and out?

The snake flicks its tongue to smell its surroundings. Because the tongue picks up tiny particles from the air and the ground and brings them to special organs in the mouth, the snake can find food and sense danger.
Why does lightning often hit tall trees or towers?

Tall trees and towers give lightning a short, easy path to the ground. Because the electricity looks for the easiest and shortest path to the ground and tall things stand closer to the cloud, they are struck more often.
Why does a glass jar sometimes crack when boiling water is poured into it straight from a cold shelf?
A sudden jump in temperature makes the glass strain unevenly. Because the inner glass swells quickly while the outer glass is still cold and small, the strain between them pulls the jar apart.
Why do parents worry when their child is late coming home?

Parents worry when they do not know that their child is safe. Because they care about our safety, cannot see where we are and do not know why we are late, their minds fill with possible problems until we are home.
Why does reading your own writing aloud help you spot mistakes?
Reading aloud makes us slow down and hear each word. Because our eyes tend to skip over errors when we read silently and fast, our ears notice words that sound wrong or missing.
After a hard test is over, why do we feel relieved?
Relief comes once the pressure of the test is gone. Because the mind has been tense while waiting and the worry has ended, the body relaxes.
Why does our mouth water when we smell hot pakoras?
The mouth makes more spit to get ready for food. Because the smell tells the brain that food is near, the brain signals the glands in the mouth to make spit, which helps to break down food.
Why does a tree have such thick bark?
The thick bark protects the tree. Because the tough outer layer shields the soft living wood from heat, knocks, and tiny insects, the tree can live for many years.
Why do frozen vegetables turn soft and watery after they thaw?

Freezing breaks the soft parts of vegetables, so they go mushy after thawing. Because water inside the cells turns into sharp ice crystals that break the cell walls, the pieces cannot stay firm when they warm up.
Do good friends have to agree about everything?
No, good friends do not have to agree about everything. Because a friendship rests on trust and respect and not on matching opinions, friends can disagree politely and still enjoy each other.
Why is a loose scarf a bad idea when riding on a motorbike or near a machine?
A loose scarf can get caught in moving parts. Because a flapping end may be pulled into a wheel or machine part, it can yank the wearer along with it.
Why do people stand in a queue at a crowded festival stall?
A queue keeps things fair and orderly. Because people are served in the order they came, nobody can push ahead, and there is less pushing and shouting.
Why does a house with thick walls stay cooler in summer?
Thick walls slow the heat coming in from outside. Because the heat from the sun takes a long time to travel through the wall to the inside, the rooms stay comfortable well into the afternoon.
Why does practising with the weaker hand help a player become better with both?
Practice trains the weaker hand through repetition. Because the brain and muscles get better at any movement they repeat, the weaker hand slowly catches up.
Why do we clean a wall before painting it?
We clean the wall first so the paint will last. Because paint holds well on a clean, dry surface but slips off dust or grease, a dirty wall makes the new coat peel.
Why is a house with a tin roof usually hotter inside than one with a clay-tile roof?

Tin passes the sun's heat inside much faster than clay tile does. Because metal soaks up the sun's heat and passes it straight through, while thick tiles pass it on slowly, the room under the tin heats up sooner.
Why is a room with heavy curtains and thick carpets quieter than a bare room?
Cloth and carpet soak up sound that bare surfaces would bounce back. Because soft things take in sound instead of reflecting it, there are fewer echoes and the noise dies away quickly.
Why do birds build nests?
Birds build nests to give their eggs and chicks a safe place. Because eggs need warmth and shelter and a nest keeps them off the ground, away from many dangers, more chicks survive.
Why is it better to ask the teacher when you are stuck than to guess and move on?
Asking clears up the problem at once, while a guess may leave a gap. Because a guess may be wrong and later lessons often depend on earlier ones, a small gap can grow bigger if it is left alone.
Every student who wins the quiz gets a medal. Kiran has a medal. Did Kiran win the quiz?
We cannot be sure. Because the rule says winners get medals but does not say that only winners do, Kiran may have earned his medal in another way.
Why is it fair for every person in the house to help with the chores?

Sharing the chores spreads the work across everyone who lives in the house. Because the work would pile up on one person if the rest did nothing, sharing the tasks keeps any one person from being worn out.
Why does laughing make a bad mood feel lighter?
Laughing eases worry and relaxes the body. Because it takes our attention off the problem for a moment and loosens the body, we feel better afterwards.
Why is the soil next to a river often good for farming?
River floods leave a rich layer of mud on the land that feeds crops. Because floods deposit a fine layer of silt rich in nutrients from far upstream, the plants growing there find plenty of food.
Why does a mirror show a clear picture of your face while a plain wall does not?

Smooth glass sends back a clear picture, while a rough wall does not. Because smooth glass sends light back in an orderly way, while a rough wall scatters it in all directions, only the mirror keeps the shape of your face.
Why does a fuse cut off the electricity when too much power flows through it?
A fuse protects the wires. Because too much current heats a wire and can start a fire, the thin fuse wire melts first and breaks the circuit.
Why do people tie a name tag on their luggage?
A tag helps to identify the bag. Because many bags look alike and a tag shows who owns each one, a bag that goes astray can be returned to its owner.
Why do we pull our hand away from a hot pan before we have even thought about it?

A quick reflex pulls the hand away. Because the message of heat is handled by the spinal cord, which sends back an order to move without waiting for the brain to decide, the hand is saved a moment earlier.
If a clock runs slow, will it show a time earlier or later than the real time?
A slow clock shows an earlier time. Because it ticks off time more slowly than it really passes, it falls behind the real time and so shows a time that has already gone by.
Everybody in Class A has a bicycle, and Naman has a bicycle. Is Naman in Class A?
We cannot be sure. Because the rule says that each pupil in Class A has a bicycle but does not say that only those pupils have bicycles, Naman may belong to another class.
Some of the singers in the choir are also in the drama club. Does that mean every singer is in the drama club?
No, we cannot say that. Because the word some only tells us that at least part of the choir is in the drama club, the rest of the singers may not be.
A friend says, Whenever I wear my red shirt I score well, so the shirt makes me score. Is that good reasoning?

No, it is not good reasoning. Because a shirt and a good score happening together does not show that either causes the other, the score may come from practice, luck or a good day, so we cannot say the shirt does anything.
Why do students usually think more clearly after a good night's sleep?
A rested student thinks more clearly. Because the brain needs sleep to recover its attention and to sort and store what was learned during the day, a tired mind is slower and forgets more.
Why do trekkers usually start walking early in the morning?

An early start gives trekkers the best part of the day for walking. Because the morning is cooler and the sky is usually clearer, and an early start leaves plenty of daylight to finish the walk before dark or afternoon storms, trekkers can walk safely.
Why does a room get dusty even when the windows stay shut?

Dust also comes from inside the house and from what people bring in. Because fabrics, paper and skin all shed tiny bits, and people carry fine dirt in on shoes and clothes, the bits drift in the air and settle on surfaces.
Why does a cook taste the food while it is cooking and not only at the end?

Tasting along the way lets the cook correct mistakes in time. Because the flavour is easy to adjust while the dish is still on the fire but difficult to fix after it is finished, an early taste saves the meal.
Why does a pencil leave a mark on paper?
A little of the pencil's lead wears off onto the paper. Because the soft graphite breaks into tiny flakes as it rubs over the rough surface, the flakes stay caught in the paper and form the line.
Why should hot cooked rice cool a little before it is packed into a closed box?
Rice should cool first or it will turn soggy. Because hot rice gives off steam, and the steam cools on the inside of the lid and drips back as water, the grains get wet and sticky.
Why do gardeners leave space between seedlings when they plant them?
Seedlings need space to grow well. Because each plant spreads its roots to find water and its leaves to catch light, crowded plants compete and all of them grow weak.
Why do students forget so much after a long holiday?
Memories fade when they are not used. Because every time we recall something the link in the brain gets stronger, and during a long break those links are not used, the details become harder to find.
Why does a shirt look darker when it is wet?

A wet shirt sends less light back to our eyes. Because water fills the tiny gaps between the threads and lets more of the light pass into the cloth instead of bouncing off it, less reflected light reaches us.
Why should we prepare questions before meeting an expert who visits our school?
Prepared questions make the visit more useful. Because nervousness can make us forget what we wanted to ask, a short written list helps us ask clearly and not miss the points that matter to us.
Why is it hard to follow a lesson in a noisy classroom?
Other sounds drown out the teacher's voice and pull attention away. Because the brain has to pick the teacher's voice out from all the other sounds, which takes effort, some words are missed.
Why does a sealed packet of snacks look puffed up when it is taken up a mountain?

The air inside the packet pushes outward harder than the thin air outside. Because the air sealed inside pushes outward with the same strength as at home while less air presses on it from outside, the packet swells.
Why should we pull a plug out by the plug itself and not by tugging the wire?
Pulling by the plug is safer. Because tugging the wire strains the thin wires inside and can loosen or break them, the cable can get damaged and later cause sparks or a shock.
Why does waiting for exam results seem to take so long?

Waiting feels long when our minds stay fixed on it. Because we keep thinking about the result and there is nothing we can do to change it, every moment seems stretched, while busy moments pass unnoticed.
Why is it dangerous to walk on a railway track?

A train cannot stop quickly, so a person on the track is in danger. Because a train is very heavy and needs a long distance to stop, and the driver may not see a person in time, there is no safe moment to be on the track.
Why might a child who is often teased begin to stay away from others?
The child may stay away to avoid more hurt. Because being alone feels safer than facing unkind remarks, the child pulls back, and the right response from adults is to listen and to stop the teasing.
A friend says, I never tell lies. Yesterday we heard her tell a lie to the teacher. Is her statement true?
No, her statement is not true. Because never means not even on some rare occasion, a lie told yesterday proves that her claim is wrong.
A box sits on top of a shelf, and a cat sleeps under the shelf. Is the box higher than the cat?
Yes, the box is higher than the cat. Because the box is above the shelf and the cat is below it, the shelf lies between them.
The biscuit jar was full this morning and is empty now. Bunty was home alone. Does that prove Bunty emptied it?
No, it does not prove it. Because other people might have come into the house or taken the biscuits while Bunty was busy, we only have a reason for suspicion and need more facts.
Some fruits are sweet, and a lemon is a fruit. Is a lemon sweet?
We cannot be sure from this alone. Because the first sentence says only that some fruits are sweet, it does not tell us which ones, so it cannot settle the question about a lemon.
Why is it wise to put a piece of writing aside for a while before checking it?
A break makes mistakes easier to see. Because after we have just written something, our brain fills in what we meant to say, and with some time away we read what is really on the page.
When a list of chores is long, what should be done first?
The important chores should come first. Because time or energy can run out before the list is finished, doing the key tasks early means the things that matter most are done.
Why does a drop of ink spread slowly through a glass of still water?
The ink mixes slowly into the water by itself. Because particles of a liquid are always jostling about, they slowly mix with each other, even without any stirring.
Why should a student tell the teacher early when homework cannot be finished?
Early notice keeps more choices open. Because the teacher can still offer help or extra time when there is room to adjust, while telling them at the last moment leaves little choice.
Why should students name the book when they copy a fact into their notes?

Naming the book lets others trust and check the fact. Because a reader can look the fact up in the same place and see whether it was copied correctly, and the author gets the credit for the work, it is the honest way to use it.
Why does tea stay hot for hours in a flask?

A flask slows down the escape of heat. Because the wall of the flask has an almost empty gap inside it that heat cannot cross easily, and the shiny lining reflects heat back in, very little warmth gets out.
Why is it better to begin a project early even when the deadline is far away?
An early start leaves spare time for surprises. Because unexpected problems often appear, such as missing materials or an illness, that spare time lets us deal with them without panic.
Why must a fair test change only the thing we are studying?

Keeping everything else the same lets us link the result to the thing we study. Because if other things change as well, we cannot tell which of them caused the result, the result would not teach us anything certain.
Why does water left in a dark bucket in the sun become warm?

The dark bucket soaks up the sun's energy and heats the water. Because sunlight carries energy, and a dark surface soaks up more of it than a pale surface, the bucket heats up and passes the heat to the water.
What is the use of checking pockets before clothes go into the wash?
Checking pockets avoids damage. Because a forgotten pen can leak ink over the whole wash and paper turns to bits in the water, a quick look saves the clothes and the notes.
Why do good teachers praise effort and not only high marks?

Praising effort encourages students to keep trying. Because effort is something a student can control and improve, while marks also depend on other things, praise for hard work makes them feel that progress is in their own hands.
Why does a torch grow dim after a long time of use?

The torch dims as its batteries run low. Because a battery has only a limited store of energy, and it weakens as the store is used, it pushes the current less strongly and the bulb glows less brightly.
Why must cleaning liquids stay in their own labelled bottles and never be poured into drink bottles?

A cleaning liquid in a drink bottle could be swallowed by mistake. Because a drink bottle looks harmless, while the original label warns people what is inside, the liquid should stay in its own bottle.
Why do honest people try to tell the truth even when a lie would be easier?

Honest people choose the truth to avoid the trouble that lies bring. Because a lie usually needs more lies to support it, and trust is hard to win back after it is lost, honesty saves trouble in the long run.
Why do people often feel lighter after they say sorry and mean it?
A sincere apology lifts a weight. Because it shows that we care about the person we hurt and gives them a chance to forgive, it mends trust and also eases our own guilt.
Why must the doors marked as fire exits be kept clear?
Fire exits must stay clear so people can get out fast. Because in an emergency many people need to leave at the same moment, anything that blocks the way slows everybody down and puts them in danger.
Rain is the only thing that makes the water tank overflow here. The tank is overflowing. Did it rain?
Yes, it must have rained. Because rain is the only thing that makes the tank overflow here and the tank is overflowing, the rain is the cause.
If the dog barks whenever someone is at the door, and the dog is quiet now, can we be sure nobody is at the door?
We cannot be sure. Because the rule says that a visitor makes the dog bark but not that only a visitor can do it, a quiet dog may simply not have noticed a visitor, or may be asleep.
The lake lies north of the village and the temple lies south of the village. Is the lake north of the temple?
Yes, the lake is north of the temple. Because the temple is on the south side of the village and the lake is on the north side, the village lies between them along the same line.
Ali stands in front of Beena in a queue, and Chetan stands behind Beena. Who is in the middle?
Beena is in the middle. Because Ali is ahead of her and Chetan is behind her, she stands between them.
Why is it a good idea to write a name on a lunch box?
A name helps the box get back to its owner. Because many lunch boxes look alike, a box left in a bus or a classroom could be mistaken for another, and the name tells anyone who finds it whose it is.
Why do many shoppers carry a cloth bag to the market?

A cloth bag can be used again and again. Because plastic bags are often thrown away after a short use and then pile up as rubbish, a cloth bag keeps waste low and is also strong enough for heavy things.
Why does a wooden drawer get hard to open in the rainy season?
The wood swells in damp air and sticks in its frame. Because wood takes in moisture from damp air and grows slightly larger, it fits more tightly.
Why is it a good idea to look at a route before cycling to a new place?
Looking at the route first saves trouble. Because it helps us avoid wrong turns and very busy roads, we reach the place with less stress and more safely.
Why do teachers ask students to line up calmly before entering the science lab?
A calm line keeps the lab safer. Because the teacher can check everyone and give the safety rules before anybody touches the equipment, there is less chance of pushing, spills and mistakes.
Why does a specific compliment mean more than a general compliment?
A specific compliment feels warmer. Because naming exactly what we liked shows that we really noticed and thought about it, the person feels that the praise is honest.
Why is it easier to be brave when a friend is standing beside us?
Courage comes more easily with a friend nearby. Because a familiar person calms us and we feel that we do not face the scary thing alone, the fear does not feel as large.
Why do people stuff wet shoes with newspaper to dry them?

Paper pulls water out of the wet shoes and speeds their drying. Because paper soaks up some of the moisture and keeps the inside of the shoe open so that air can move through, the water leaves faster.
Why should a child tell a trusted adult where they are going when they go out to play?
Telling an adult means help can be found quickly. Because the adult then knows where to look if plans change or something goes wrong, a problem does not stay hidden for long.
Why do students use ruled paper when they practise handwriting?
Ruled paper helps keep the writing neat. Because the lines give the eye something to follow and show how tall each letter should be, the writing stays straight and even.
Why should we change a plan when the situation changes?
An old plan may no longer fit the new situation. Because it was made for the earlier situation, sticking to it may lead us to a result we no longer want, while a quick adjustment keeps us on track.
Why do people tend to speak louder in a noisy place?
People speak louder in noise to be heard. Because the background sound covers their voice, they raise it to reach the listener, often without noticing how loud they have become.
Why is it hard to listen to criticism even when it is fair?
Even fair criticism can sting. Because being judged makes us feel defensive before we have time to think, and it touches our pride, even fair remarks hurt until the first reaction passes.
Why does a bicycle tyre go soft slowly even when it has no puncture?
Air slowly seeps out through the rubber and the valve. Because rubber is not perfectly airtight and the valve is not either, a little air escapes all the time.
Why do tall buildings have a metal rod fixed to the top?

The rod protects the building from lightning. Because it gives a lightning strike an easy path through a thick wire to the ground, the electricity does not pass through the building's walls and the people inside.
Why do games need rules that everyone agrees to?
Games need agreed rules so that play is fair. Because without them players would disagree about what is allowed and who has won, the rules make sure that everyone is playing the same game.
In the evening the sun is setting on my right-hand side. Which way am I facing?
You are facing south. Because the sun sets in the west and it is on your right side, the south must be straight ahead of you.
Sam or Tina ate the last laddoo, and nobody else was at home. Tina honestly says she did not eat it. Who did?
Sam ate it. Because the laddoo was eaten by Sam or Tina, and Tina says honestly that it was not her, only Sam remains.
The map shows a river between a village and a town. Can the villagers simply walk in a straight line from the village to the town?
Not necessarily. Because a river blocks a walker unless there is a bridge or a shallow place to cross, the villagers may have to go around to reach the other side.
Nobody in the room is wearing a hat, and Tara is in the room. Is Tara wearing a hat?
No, Tara is not wearing a hat. Because nobody in the room wears a hat and Tara is in the room, she cannot be an exception.
Why is it useful to keep a first-aid box at home?
A first-aid box keeps bandages and clean dressings in a known place. Because small accidents happen without warning, a small cut or scrape can then be cleaned and covered right away.
Why do a cat's eyes seem to glow when torchlight falls on them at night?

A mirror-like layer at the back of a cat's eye sends light back out. Because that layer reflects light so the eye gets a second chance to catch it, some of that light comes straight back to the person holding the torch.
Why does a cake rise in the oven?

Gas bubbles form in the batter and puff it up as it bakes. Because the raising ingredient gives off gas and the heat makes the bubbles swell, the batter sets around them, which leaves it soft and full of tiny holes.
Why do cars have seat belts?

Seat belts keep people from being thrown forward. Because the body keeps moving at the car's speed even when the car stops suddenly, the belt holds the person against the seat and spreads the force across the strong parts of the body.
Why is a person in trouble more likely to get help when we ask a particular person than when we call out to a crowd?
Asking a particular person works better. Because in a crowd everyone may assume somebody else will step in, nobody does, while a person who is named directly knows that the job is theirs.
Why can music change our mood so quickly?
Music acts on both the body and memory. Because the rhythm and tune make us move, breathe and feel in time with them, and a song can also bring back happy or sad memories, the feeling shifts.
Why do we shake a bottle of salad dressing before using it?
Shaking mixes the dressing again. Because oil and vinegar do not stay mixed and settle into layers, shaking spreads them evenly through the liquid so each spoonful tastes right.
Why is it hard to study when a phone keeps buzzing nearby?

A buzzing phone breaks our concentration. Because every buzz pulls attention away, and the mind needs time to settle back into the task after each interruption, work gets slower and mistakes creep in.
Why should a group agree on a meeting place before going to a crowded fair?
A meeting place helps people who get separated. Because a crowd makes it easy to lose each other, and phones may not work in the noise, everyone knows where to go to find the others.
Why does cooked food keep longer in a closed box than on an open plate?
A lid protects the food from things that spoil it. Because the lid keeps out flies, dust and germs and slows the drying of the food, it stays good for longer.
Why do elephants flap their large ears?
Flapping helps an elephant cool down. Because the ears are thin and full of blood vessels, air blowing over them cools the blood, and the cooler blood then travels back through the body.
Why should we tell an adult when a friend says something that makes us worry about their safety?

Telling an adult is the right step. Because an adult has more experience and more ways to help, and keeping the worry secret leaves our friend alone with the problem, the friend is better off when someone responsible knows.
Why does laughter spread so quickly in a group of friends?

People catch each other's moods, so one laugh sets others off. Because we copy the faces and sounds of those around us without noticing, and a laugh makes the mood feel light, the laughing passes from person to person.
Why does a heavy bag feel heavier near the end of a long walk?
A tired carrier finds the same weight harder to hold. Because the muscles that hold it up use up their energy and grow weaker as time passes, the same weight takes more effort.
Why does a friendly smile make a stranger easier to approach?
A smile makes a person seem approachable. Because it is a widely understood sign that someone means no harm, the other person feels safer and more willing to talk.
Why does a student who reads a little every day usually remember more than a student who crams the night before a test?
Reading a little each day works better. Because the brain stores facts more firmly when it meets them again after gaps of time, regular short sessions build a stronger memory than a rushed night.
Which word does not belong with the others: cup, plate, bowl, hammer?
The hammer does not belong. Because a cup, a plate and a bowl are all used for eating or drinking, while a hammer is a tool for hitting nails.
Anju always arrives before Ben, and Ben always arrives before Cara. If Cara arrived early today, did Anju also arrive early?
Yes, Anju arrived early too. Because Anju always comes before Ben and Ben comes before Cara, Anju must have arrived even earlier than Cara.
Riya says her brother is taller than she is, and her brother says that Riya is taller than he is. Can they be telling the truth together?
No, they cannot be right together. Because the brother cannot be taller than Riya while Riya is taller than the brother, the statements contradict each other.
Every mango in the basket is ripe, and Lata takes a mango out of the basket. Is her mango ripe?
Yes, her mango is ripe. Because every mango in the basket is ripe and hers came from the basket, it must be among the ripe ones.
Why is it smart to pack the school bag in the evening instead of the morning?
Packing the night before is smarter. Because mornings are rushed and a missing book or a lost sock is hard to look for in a hurry, an evening check leaves time to find what we need.
Why do slices of cucumber become watery when we sprinkle salt on them?
The salt pulls water out of the cucumber. Because water tends to move toward the saltier side, the strong salt on the surface draws it out of the cells, and it collects as drops.
Why does a river rush faster in the hills than on the plains?

The land slopes steeply in the hills and gently on the plains. Because gravity pulls the water downhill harder along a steep slope and the water has little to hold it back, it speeds up, while on flat land it slows and spreads out.
Why might a friend go quiet for a while after a quarrel?
A quiet pause gives strong feelings time to settle. Because speaking while still angry or hurt can lead to saying things we regret, some people prefer to stay silent until they feel calmer.
Why can bats fly in the dark without bumping into things?
Bats find their way by sound. Because a bat makes high squeaks and listens for the echoes that bounce back from objects, it can tell where things are even when it cannot see them.
Why do we feel proud after we finish something that was hard for us?
Pride comes from seeing what our effort achieved. Because the hard work led to a real result, we notice that our skill has grown, and that discovery feels good.
Why should a pot on the stove never be left alone for long?

Things can go wrong quickly on a stove, so someone should stay nearby. Because food can boil over onto the flame or boil dry and burn, and a fire can start when nobody is there to stop it, a pot should not be left alone.
Is it unkind to laugh at a person who has tripped and fallen, even when it looks funny?
Yes, it can be unkind. Because the person may be hurt and embarrassed, our laughter makes the embarrassment worse, while checking whether they are all right shows care.
Why is a globe a truer model of the Earth than a flat map?

A globe keeps the shapes and sizes of lands better than a flat map. Because the Earth is shaped like a ball, and a ball cannot be laid flat without stretching or cutting it, a flat map has to distort some lands.
Why does paper tear more easily along a line where it has been folded?
The fold weakens the paper, so the tear follows it. Because folding bends and strains the fibres along the line, the paper is weaker there.
Why do some people keep a bowl of water outside for birds in the hot season?

The bowl gives thirsty birds a safe place to drink and cool off. Because puddles and streams dry up in a hot season and birds need water for drinking and for keeping cool, a clean bowl in a shady place helps them.
Why do woollen clothes keep us warm in winter?
Wool holds body heat close to the skin. Because the fibres trap a lot of air among them, and still air passes heat along very poorly, the warmth of the body stays in.
Why can old friends understand each other with very little talking?
Old friends read small signals easily. Because they have a long shared past and have seen each other in many situations, a small look or a short remark carries a lot of meaning to them.
Why does pickle keep for a long time in a jar?
Salt, oil and acid make pickle a hard place for germs to grow. Because most germs cannot live in this mix, and germs are what spoil food, the pickle stays good for much longer than fresh vegetables.
Why do far-off hills look blue and hazy?

The air between us and distant hills tints them blue and pale. Because the air scatters the blue part of sunlight more than the other colours and adds this scattered light to what we see, the farther the hill, the bluer and paler it appears.
Why do people feel jealous sometimes, and is it wrong to feel that way?

Jealousy is a common feeling and having it is not wrong. Because we want something another person has or fear losing someone's attention, the feeling comes up on its own, and what matters is how we act on it.
Everyone who came to the party brought a gift. Zoya did not bring a gift. Did Zoya come to the party?
No, Zoya did not come. Because anyone who came brought a gift and Zoya brought none, she cannot have been there.
If the shop is open, its light is on. The light is on. Is the shop open?
We cannot be sure. Because the rule only says that an open shop has its light on, the light might also have been left on while the shop is closed.
All cats are animals. Does that mean all animals are cats?
No, not all animals are cats. Because the statement only places cats inside the larger group of animals, there is room in that group for dogs, cows, birds and many others.
A bag contains only red balls. Can Pooja draw a blue ball from it?
No, she cannot draw a blue ball. Because the bag holds only red balls, no blue ball is there to be drawn.
Why do fireflies glow in the evening?

Fireflies glow to send signals to each other. Because the glow is made by a chemical reaction inside their bodies and each kind flashes in its own pattern, other fireflies can recognise and find a mate.
Why should we never look straight at the sun?

Looking at the sun can damage the eyes. Because its strong light falls on the delicate part at the back of the eye that senses light, and that part can be harmed even if it does not hurt at that moment, the eye should be protected.
Why do some people prefer a quiet evening at home to a big party?

People differ in how they get their energy. Because some people feel drained by crowds and noise, while others feel lively, a quiet evening can be restful for some people, while a party suits others better.
Why does a map have a key?

A map has a key to explain its symbols. Because the symbols are only drawings that stand for things like roads, rivers and schools, a reader who does not know the meaning would have to guess, and the key tells them.
Why does ironing make crumpled clothes smooth?

Ironing resets the cloth's fibres into a flat shape. Because warmth makes the fibres soft and willing to move, and the weight of the iron presses them flat as they cool, the cloth keeps the smooth shape.
Why is it good to turn off the tap while brushing our teeth?
Turning off the tap saves water. Because running water keeps flowing whether we use it or not, closing the tap lets us use only what we need for rinsing.
Why does the sun seem to rise in the east?

The sun only seems to move; the Earth turning towards the east brings the sun into view from the east. Because our own spot is carried around with the spinning Earth, we are turned toward the sun in the morning from that side, and it appears to climb into the sky.
Why do electricians use screwdrivers with plastic or rubber handles?
The handles protect the hand. Because rubber and plastic do not let electricity flow through them easily, a current in the metal cannot reach the person's hand, and the handle also gives a good grip.
Why does it hurt when friends plan an outing and do not invite us?
