Being left out feels like losing a place that matters to us. Because people have a deep need to belong to a group, the hurt comes even when no harm was meant.
Why does food take longer to cook on a high mountain?

Water boils at a lower temperature on a mountain, so food cooks slowly. Because the air pressure is lower there, the boiling water is not as hot, and water that is not as hot cooks the food more slowly.
Why do we remember embarrassing moments so clearly for years?
Embarrassing moments are stored more firmly than ordinary ones. Because they stir strong feelings, and we replay them again and again in our minds, the memory stays sharp.
Why should an electric heater never be used to dry clothes by draping them over it?

Cloth on a hot heater can catch fire, and a covered heater can overheat. Because cloth touching or close to a hot heater can heat up until it ignites, and a covered heater cannot let its own heat escape, both dangers are real.
If a classmate stays silent when we greet them, does that prove they are being rude?
No, it does not prove that. Because many things can explain silence, such as shyness, worry, not hearing us or thinking about something else, it is fairer to ask kindly than to decide they are rude.
Why do birds fluff up their feathers on a cold morning?
Fluffed feathers keep a bird warmer. Because puffing them up traps more air close to the body, and still air is a poor carrier of heat, less warmth escapes from the bird.
Why do stars twinkle while planets shine steadily?

Starlight is shaken on its way to us, while planet light is steadier. Because a star is so far away that it is a tiny point and the moving layers of our air shift that point about, while a planet is a larger disc and looks steadier, stars flicker and planets do not.
Why do group projects sometimes go wrong when nobody decides who does what?
Unclear roles make a group project go wrong. Because each person can assume that someone else is looking after a task, some jobs get done by many people and others by nobody.
Fish is to water as bird is to what?
The answer is air. Because a fish lives and moves in water, in the same way a bird lives and flies in the air.
Why does a woollen sweater shrink when it is washed in very hot water?

Hot water makes the wool fibres tighten and tangle. Because the heat and the rubbing in the wash make the tiny scales on the fibres lock together, the cloth pulls in and cannot return to its old size.
A friend saw the cricket match herself. Another friend only heard about it from someone else. Whose account is likely to be more reliable?

The friend who saw it herself is likely to be more reliable. Because she watched the events directly, her account has not passed through anyone else, while a story heard second-hand can be changed or mixed up on the way.
Why should we leave home earlier than needed on the day of an exam?
Leaving early is sensible. Because buses can be late and roads can be blocked, extra time means that a delay does not make us miss the start of the exam.
Why does the smell of perfume seem to fade after a while even though it is still there?

The nose gets used to a scent and stops reporting it. Because the smell cells send weaker signals when they meet the same scent again and again, the brain stops noticing it, while someone who has just walked in still smells it.
Why do cracks appear in a muddy field in a long dry spell?
The drying mud shrinks and splits into pieces. Because the water leaving the soil makes it pull together, and the surface cannot shrink evenly, cracks open.
Why do window panes rattle during a loud clap of thunder?
Loud thunder shakes the glass in its frame. Because a loud sound is a series of strong pressure changes in the air, and the thin glass is pushed back and forth by them, it vibrates.
Why do the heels of shoes usually wear out first?

Heels take the hardest knock and the most rubbing at each step. Because the heel is the part that lands on the ground first and carries the weight of the body, it rubs against the ground more than the rest of the sole.
Why is it sometimes hard to say no to a friend?
Fear of letting a friend down makes saying no hard. Because we value the friendship and worry that a refusal might upset them or spoil the bond, we may agree even when we do not want to.
Why do cooks keep stirring a pot of thick soup?
Stirring keeps the soup from burning. Because the bottom of the pot gets the most heat, soup that stays there can stick and scorch, and stirring moves it around and spreads the heat evenly.
Why should the handle of a pan on the stove be turned inward?
Turning the handle in keeps it out of the way of passing arms. Because a knocked pan tips hot food onto people, and a handle that sticks out is easy to knock, keeping it inward lowers the risk.
Why does a rumour spread so fast?

People pass surprising news on before checking it. Because people like to share surprising news, each person who hears it passes it on without checking whether it is true, and the story is often made more exciting on the way.
Why is it wise to wait before replying to an angry message?
A short pause lets anger fade before we reply. Because strong anger makes us choose harsher words than we really mean, waiting lets us calm down and write a reply that is less likely to hurt.
Why can we smell flowers more strongly on a warm morning than on a cold morning?
Warm air carries more scent to our noses. Because heat helps the scent particles escape from the petals and drift through the air faster, more of them reach us.
Why do cows swish their tails again and again?
Cows swish their tails to chase away flies. Because flies land on the skin and bite or tickle, and the tail is the part that can reach most of the body, a swish drives them off.
Why is a car that has stood in the sun with its windows shut so hot inside?

The sun's heat gets trapped inside the shut car. Because sunlight passes through the glass and warms the seats and the inside of the car, and the warmed things give off heat that cannot easily get back out through the glass, the air inside heats up.
Why does handwriting get messy when we write in a hurry?
Hurried writing has less control, so the letters lose their shape. Because the hand has less time to guide each stroke when it moves fast, the lines wander.
Every time Uma washes her scooter, it rains. Does washing the scooter make it rain?
No, washing does not cause rain. Because things that happen together do not prove that the first causes the second, the rain comes from the weather, and the washing is just a coincidence.
Why is it useful to keep important papers in the same place at home?

Keeping papers together in a fixed place saves time. Because we will know where to look when we need them in a hurry, we do not waste time searching or risk losing a document that cannot be replaced easily.
Why does the water in a deep well stay cool even in the hot season?
The ground deep down stays cool all summer, and so does the well water. Because the heat of the sun hardly reaches far below the surface, the water deep in the well stays cool.
Why does a bell go on ringing for a while after it has been struck?

The metal keeps shaking for a while after the blow. Because the blow sets the whole metal body vibrating and the vibration only dies down slowly, the shaking air carries the sound to our ears for some time.
Why does a gift feel special when the giver remembered something we like?
Such a gift shows that the giver paid attention to us. Because we can tell that they thought about us and not just about buying something, we feel noticed and cared for.
Why does an iron nail left out in the rain turn reddish-brown?
The nail is rusting. Because iron slowly joins with oxygen when water is present, it forms a reddish-brown flaky coating called rust.
Why do we feel chilly when we step out of a swimming pool, even on a warm day?
Water drying on the skin cools the body. Because water that turns to vapour takes heat from the skin as it leaves, the wet body loses warmth faster than a dry body.
Why can we shape wet sand into a castle but not dry sand?
Water between the grains lets wet sand hold a shape. Because a thin film of water pulls neighbouring grains toward each other, they stick, while dry grains just slide apart.
Why can good friends disagree even when they like each other very much?

Liking someone does not make people think alike, so even good friends disagree. Because each person has different wishes and opinions, disagreements will happen, and talking about them calmly can even make a friendship stronger.
Why does ghee turn solid in the winter?
Ghee sets firm when the air is cold. Because its fats stay liquid only when they are warm enough, and cooler air takes away their heat, they thicken and become firm.
Why does cooking oil start to smoke when it gets too hot?

Oil smokes when it is heated past what it can stand. Because heat beyond that point splits its substances into vapours, smoke rises from the pan, and the oil can then catch fire, so the pan must be taken off the heat.
Why might children feel sad when their favourite teacher leaves the school?
The children feel the loss of a person who mattered to them. Because they formed a bond with someone who encouraged them every day, they miss the support and the routine they shared.
Why does the sea rise and fall at the shore each day?
The moon's pull on the oceans makes the tides. Because the moon's gravity tugs on the water as the Earth turns, the water heaps up on some shores and draws back from others.
Why is it kind to ask before taking someone's photograph?
Asking shows respect for the person in the picture. Because everyone has a right to decide how their face is shared, and some people may not want to be photographed, a question lets them choose.
Why do we feel awkward when we forget the name of someone we have met before?
Forgetting a name can seem like a sign that we did not care. Because a name is part of how people feel known and remembered, we worry about hurting the person, even when we did care.
Why can a parrot say words it has heard?

A parrot copies sounds it hears, including words. Because parrots are very good at imitating what they hear and often copy the voices of the people who live with them, they learn to repeat words without knowing what they mean.
Why does a fan make us feel cooler even though it does not cool the air?
A fan helps us feel cooler by helping sweat dry. Because moving air carries away the moisture on our skin and the drying takes heat from the body, we feel cooler even though the air is no colder.
If I stand facing north and turn to my right, which direction am I facing?
You would be facing east. Because east lies to the right of north when we go around the compass the way a clock's hands move, turning right from north brings us to the east.
Why does it help to read the whole question before starting to write an answer?

Reading the whole question helps us answer what is really asked. Because the last words often add a condition or a limit, a student who starts after reading only the first part may write a good answer to the wrong question.
Why is it a good habit to put things back where they belong?
Putting things back saves time. Because we will know where to look the next time we need them, and nobody else has to search either, little things do not get lost.
Why does smoke from a fire rise?
Hot air carries the smoke upward. Because hot air is lighter than the cooler air around it, it floats upward and takes the smoke with it.
Why is the ground cooler under a big tree in summer?

The tree's shade and cool leaves keep the ground below cooler. Because the leaves block much of the sunlight and the tree also gives off water vapour from its leaves, which cools the air around them, the spot stays pleasant.
Why do old photographs fade when they are left in the sunlight?
Strong light bleaches the colours in photographs. Because the energy in sunlight slowly damages the dyes that make the picture, the colours become paler year after year.
Why does a baby smile back when we smile at it?

A baby answers a friendly face with a smile of its own. Because babies learn about the world by watching the faces of people around them and a smile signals safety and warmth, they soon answer it in the same way.
Why does an empty room echo more than a room full of furniture?
Bare walls and floors bounce sound back, so an empty room echoes. Because curtains, sofas and rugs are soft and soak up part of the sound, a furnished room sends much less of it back to our ears.
Why do we trust a friend who has always kept their promises?
Past behaviour is the best clue we have about what a person will do. Because a person who has kept their word many times has shown that they care about doing so, we expect them to do the same again.
Why do young children enjoy pretend games such as playing shop or doctor?
Pretend play helps children learn about the world. Because they can try out roles, talk the way grown-ups do and practise solving little problems in a safe way, they understand how people behave.
Why does milk suddenly rush over the rim of the pot when it boils?
A skin on top of the milk holds the rising foam. Because the skin traps the steam bubbles that are rising from below, the bubbles lift the whole layer up and over the edge in a moment.
Why do many birds sing loudly at dawn?
Birds sing at dawn to mark their territory and attract mates. Because the air is calm in the early morning and the sound carries far, their calls are easy to hear.
Why should we not feed wild monkeys?

Feeding wild monkeys makes them bold and sometimes aggressive towards people. Because they soon learn to link people with food and lose their fear, they may grab bags and snatch food, and sometimes they bite.
Why do we often feel nervous just before we speak in front of the whole class?

Stress hormones make the heart race and the hands shake before we speak to the class. Because the body treats the moment as a challenge and we care what others will think of us, the feeling is strong.
Why do owls hunt at night while sparrows sleep?
Owls are built for hunting in the dark. Because their big eyes gather dim light and their hearing is very sharp, they can find mice and insects at night when most other birds are asleep.
Why do we squint when the sun is very bright?
Squinting cuts down the glare. Because narrowing the eyelids lets less light into the eye, it helps us see in strong light and protects the eye a little.
Why is a person who admits a mistake often easier to trust?

An admission shows that we can expect honesty from that person. Because it shows that the person is honest even when it is uncomfortable, we can believe that they will tell us the truth in future as well.
Why is it rude to interrupt someone who is speaking?
Interrupting treats the speaker's words as unimportant. Because the speaker loses their train of thought and may not get to finish, the talk becomes frustrating for them.
Why should a seed be planted in damp soil and not left on a dry shelf?
A seed sprouts only when it gets water. Because water soaks into the seed and wakes up the tiny plant inside, damp soil lets it start growing, while a dry shelf keeps it sleeping.
Ravi says that every dog on his street barks. Pepper is a dog on his street and she never barks. Is Ravi right?
No, Ravi is not right. Because a dog that never barks is enough to show that not every dog barks, his statement is false.
Why does a bicycle speed up when it rolls down a slope without pedalling?
Gravity pulls the bicycle downhill and speeds it up. Because gravity keeps adding a push in the direction of the slope and little friction works against it, the bicycle gains speed.
How does a daily timetable work better with gaps left for rest?
Short breaks absorb delays and keep a tired mind working well. Because tasks often take longer than expected and a tired mind works badly, gaps keep delays from piling up and help us do better work.
Why does a whiteboard marker dry out if the cap is left off?
The liquid in the ink escapes into the air from the open tip. Because that liquid turns into vapour in open air, what is left is too dry to write.
Why do all the players of a team wear shirts of the same colour?
Matching shirts help everybody tell who plays for which side. Because players, umpires and the crowd can then see at a glance who is a teammate and who is an opponent, the game is easier to follow.
Why does the smell of cooking spread right through the house?
Tiny particles of food drift through the air. Because the particles move about on their own and are carried along by every small current in the room, they reach other rooms and our noses.
Why does a crying baby often calm down when it is picked up and held?
A held baby feels safer. Because being close to a caring person's warmth and heartbeat tells the baby it is not alone, and being picked up shows that its cry was heard, the baby relaxes.
Why does a kind word from a friend lift our mood?
A kind word makes us feel valued and eases worry. Because people need to feel that others accept them, a warm remark brings the pleasant feeling of belonging.
Why does a paper boat sink after floating for a while?
The paper boat soaks up water and goes limp. Because wet paper becomes heavy and loses its stiffness, the sides sag, and water flows in over the edge.
Why can we sometimes see the moon in the daytime?

The moon is sometimes above the horizon during the day. Because the moon travels around the Earth and rises at different hours from day to day, and sunlight on its surface is bright enough to see, it can show up against the blue sky.
Why does a team usually do better when its members listen to each other?

Listening lets a team use everyone's ideas and avoid clashes. Because ideas are shared, mistakes are noticed early and nobody works against the others by accident, the team uses all its members' knowledge.
Why should a child ask an adult before taking any medicine?

Asking an adult is safer. Because the wrong medicine, or the wrong amount, can harm a child, and an adult can read the label and check with a doctor or pharmacist, the choice is made with proper knowledge.
Why does blowing across the top of an empty bottle make a humming sound?

The hum comes from the air inside the bottle. Because the stream of air across the opening makes the air in the bottle vibrate, and the size of the bottle decides which note is loudest, we hear a steady tone.
Why does a spinning coin finally fall flat on the table?
The coin loses its spin and falls. Because friction with the table and the air takes away the energy of the spin, it can no longer stay upright, and it wobbles and drops.
Why does a tiger have stripes?
The stripes help a tiger hide. Because the dark stripes break up the outline of its body among tall grass and the shadows of leaves, its prey finds it hard to see until it is close.
Why do our cheeks turn red when we are embarrassed?
More blood flows to the skin of the face when we are embarrassed. Because a rush of strong feeling makes the tiny blood vessels there widen, the skin shows the colour of the blood.
Why do shadows grow long in the late afternoon?

A low sun throws long shadows. Because light from a low sun reaches objects at a slant, it stretches their shadows far across the ground, while from high overhead it falls almost straight down and the shadow stays short.
Why might a person refuse help even when they really need it?
A person may refuse help out of pride or worry. Because they may not want to seem weak or may feel that they are a burden to others, they say no, even when help would make things easier.
Why do flower pots need small holes at the bottom?
The holes let extra water drain out. Because roots need air as well as water, and soil that stays soggy leaves no room for air, roots in a pot without holes can start to rot.
If the bell rings, school ends. School has not ended yet. Has the bell rung?
No, the bell has not rung. Because school would have ended if the bell had rung, and it has not ended, the bell cannot have rung yet.
Why do people wear layers of clothes on a mountain walk?
Layers work better than a thick garment. Because the weather and our own body heat change during the walk, we can take off a layer when we are warm and put it on again when the wind turns cold.
Why does a hot road seem to shine like water far ahead in the afternoon?

The shine is a trick of light, not real water. Because the air touching the hot road is much hotter than the air above it and bends light coming down from the sky back up to our eyes, we see a patch of sky that looks like a puddle.
Why is it good manners to say thank you when someone helps us?
Saying thank you shows that we noticed the help. Because people like to know that their effort mattered, thanks makes them feel respected and more willing to help again.
Why does a hot pan sizzle when a drop of water falls onto it?
The drop turns to steam almost instantly. Because the metal is far hotter than the water's boiling point, the water boils away in an instant, and the bursting bubbles make the noise.
Why do exam halls have a clock on the wall?
The clock lets students watch the time for themselves. Because they can see how much time is left without interrupting anyone, they can plan how long to spend on each question.
Why does telling an angry person to calm down often make them angrier?
The remark often makes anger worse. Because those words can sound as if the person's feelings do not matter, they feel unheard and more upset, while listening first helps the feeling to ease.
Why does a plant on a sunny window sill dry out faster than a plant in a shady corner?
Sun and moving air pull water out of the window plant's soil and leaves more quickly. Because warmth makes water leave faster, the plant in sunshine needs water sooner.
Why do teams often work better when each member knows their own job?
Clear jobs prevent confusion. Because nobody has to guess who will do what, the work is shared out and nothing is left undone or done again.
Tara will go to the park if the weather is fine. The weather is not fine. Will Tara go to the park?
We cannot be sure. Because the statement tells us what she does when it is fine and nothing about bad weather, she might still go for another reason.
Some of the neighbours play the flute. Priya is a neighbour. Does Priya play the flute?
The facts do not tell us. Because only some neighbours play the flute and nothing says which, Priya may or may not be among them.
Why is it better to disagree about the idea rather than attack the person?
Talking about the idea keeps the discussion fair. Because an attack makes the other person defend themselves instead of thinking, the real question is lost.
Why should we ask before borrowing something from a classmate?
Asking lets the owner say yes or no. Because the thing belongs to the classmate and they may need it, taking it quietly can cause worry and spoil trust.
A club meets on Mondays and Thursdays. Today is Wednesday. Does the club meet today?
No, the club does not meet today. Because Wednesday is neither Monday nor Thursday, it falls outside its meeting days.
Why do crowds sometimes move in the same direction without anyone leading them?
Each person follows those in front. Because it seems safe to go where others are going, the nearby people copy each other and the whole crowd flows alike.
Some dogs are brown. All brown things in the room were washed. Were all the dogs washed?
No, we cannot say so. Because the statement covers only brown things in the room, any dog that is not brown, or is not in the room, is left out of it.
Why does a person who is told they are talented sometimes stop trying hard?
They may begin to believe the skill is fixed. Because they fear that a failure would prove the praise wrong, they avoid hard tasks instead of practising.
Why does an iron-box press wrinkles out of cotton clothes?
Heat and weight smooth the cloth. Because warmth makes the fibres relax and the flat plate presses them straight, they set in that shape as the cloth cools.
Why do we sometimes feel sad when a happy event, like a school year, comes to an end?
The ending also means leaving things we liked. Because we have grown fond of the people and routines, losing them can bring sadness alongside the pride.
Why does a chimney let smoke rise out of a kitchen?
Hot smoke rises. Because warm air is lighter than the cool air around it, it floats up the tall tube and takes the smoke out.
Why do umbrellas keep us dry while a thin cloth does not?
The umbrella is made of a material that water cannot soak through. Because the fabric is tightly woven and coated, the raindrops roll off, whereas a thin cloth soaks up the water and lets it pass.
Why does homesickness often ease after a few weeks in a new place?
The new place becomes familiar. Because the child learns the routines, meets people and finds things to enjoy, the pull of home feels weaker and the days feel more settled.
Why do wet shoes smell after a rainy day if they are kept in a closed cupboard?
Dampness lets germs grow. Because the closed space keeps the moisture in, the shoes cannot dry and the microbes produce a musty smell.
Why does a bicycle chain need oil?
Oil lets the links slide easily. Because metal parts rub against each other as the chain turns, a thin layer of oil cuts down wear and noise.
Why does worry about a test often feel worse at night?
At night there is little to distract the mind. Because the house is quiet and we are tired, thoughts keep returning to the worry and it feels bigger than it is.
Why does the kitchen drain smell worse in hot weather?
Heat speeds up the growth of germs. Because food scraps in the pipe rot faster when it is warm, they give off stronger smells.
Why does a marble roll a long way on a smooth floor but not on a carpet?
The carpet slows the marble. Because its soft fibres push back against the ball and rub against it, the marble loses its speed much sooner than on a smooth floor.
Why does a vacuum flask keep tea warm for hours?
The flask stops heat from escaping. Because the flask's wall has almost no air between its layers, little heat can travel out, and the shiny lining sends the heat back in.
Why is it kind to wait until a speaker finishes before we answer?
Waiting shows respect and helps us answer properly. Because we cannot understand the whole point until it is complete, a quick reply may miss what the speaker meant.
If you plant a seed and water it, it may sprout. A seed did not sprout. Was it certainly not watered?
No, we cannot conclude that. Because sprouting depends on other things as well, such as warmth and a living seed, a lack of sprouting does not prove that watering was missed.
A box is labelled mixed fruit, but every label in the shop is wrong. What does the label tell us about the contents?
The box does not hold mixed fruit. Because every label is wrong, the words on it cannot describe what is inside.
Why is it hard to believe a person who has been caught exaggerating before?

A person who has exaggerated before makes us check everything they say. Because trust is built by being right over time, and their past words did not match the facts, a habit of stretching the truth makes them hard to believe.
Why are children usually quicker than adults at making friends in a new place?
Children are less worried about how they look to others. Because they simply start playing and invite others in, shared games turn strangers into friends before long.
No bird in the zoo is a mammal. Bats are mammals. Are there bats among the birds in the zoo?
No, there are no bats among the birds. Because the rule says that none of the birds is a mammal and a bat is a mammal, a bat cannot be counted among them.
Why do we tend to trust a person who looks us in the eye when they speak?
Eye contact suggests that the speaker has nothing to hide. Because people who avoid looking at us are often uncomfortable, steady eye contact feels honest, though it is not proof of honesty.
The sweet seller says that all his laddus are made with ghee. A customer finds a laddu that has no ghee. What follows?
The seller's statement is wrong. Because even a laddu without ghee contradicts the claim that all of them have it, the claim cannot be true.
Why do we feel restless when we wait for important news?
The mind keeps looking for an answer. Because the outcome matters and we cannot change it, the energy has nowhere to go and we fidget or pace.
Why does a knot hold when we pull on the rope?
Friction grips the rope. Because the strands press on each other where they cross, pulling only tightens the hold rather than loosening it.
Why does it help to write down what is bothering us?
Writing helps sort the jumble of thoughts. Because words on paper turn a vague feeling into something we can look at, the problem often seems clearer and easier to handle.
Why do cupboard doors sometimes spring open if they are overstuffed?
The clothes inside push outward. Because the stuffed items press against the door with more force than the latch can hold, the door gives way.
Why does a bicycle stay upright when it moves but not when it is still?
Movement helps the rider keep balance. Because the spinning wheels resist tipping and the rider can steer under any lean, a moving bicycle can stay up.
Why do we sometimes cry when we are very happy?
Strong feelings of any kind can bring tears. Because the body reacts to a surge of emotion, joy can overflow in the same way sadness does.
Why does a sewing needle have a thin point and a hole at the other end?
The point pushes through the cloth and the hole carries the thread. Because the thread follows behind the needle, the stitch is pulled in as the needle passes.
Why does wood swell during the rainy season so that doors become hard to close?
Wood takes up moisture from the air and grows a little wider. Because the fibres take in the water and swell, the door becomes a little too big for its frame.
Why is it hard to concentrate when we are very excited about something coming up?
Excitement fills the mind. Because our thoughts keep jumping to the event, less attention is left for the task in front of us.
Why does a ramp make it easier to push a heavy box onto a truck?
A ramp spreads the lifting over a longer path. Because the box rises slowly along the slope instead of straight up, each push needs less force, though the distance pushed is greater.
Why does a lighthouse have a very strong light at the top of a tall tower?
The height lets the light be seen far away. Because the tower lifts the lamp above the waves and the curve of the sea, ships far off can see it.
Why are rock pools left behind by the tide full of small creatures?
The pools trap seawater and the animals in it. Because the water stays in the hollows when the tide goes out, the creatures wait there until the sea returns.
Why does a surprise party need the guest of honour to be kept in the dark?
The surprise only works if the guest does not expect it. Because anyone who hears about it beforehand can no longer feel astonished, a leak spoils the fun of the moment.
All cats in the street are friendly. This animal is not friendly. Is it a cat from the street?
No, it is not a cat from the street. Because every cat there is friendly, an animal that is not friendly cannot be among those cats.
All the birds in the cage can sing. Pinto is in the cage. What can we tell about Pinto?
If Pinto is a bird, Pinto can sing. Because the rule covers only the birds in the cage, we need to know that Pinto is a bird before we can use it.
Why does praise work better when it names exactly what we did well?
Specific praise tells us what to repeat. Because a vague compliment gives no clue about the good part, a named detail shows that the speaker really noticed our effort.
Why does a teacher who greets pupils at the door often have a calmer class?
A warm greeting makes each pupil feel noticed. Because pupils who feel welcome settle down more easily, the lesson begins in a friendly mood.
If it is a holiday, the market is crowded. The market is crowded. Is it a holiday?
We cannot be sure. Because crowds can gather for a festival, a sale or a weekend as well, a crowded market does not by itself prove a holiday.
Why do we feel more comfortable with a new group after we have shared a task with them?
Working together gives people something in common. Because shared effort creates trust and a few jokes to remember, strangers start to feel like teammates.
Every key on the ring opens a lock in the shop. Does every lock in the shop have a key on the ring?
Not necessarily. Because the statement tells us that each key opens a lock, it does not say that each lock has a key, so some locks may need keys from elsewhere.
Why do travellers keep a spare copy of their tickets in a different place?
The spare copy protects against loss. Because a bag with the original might be stolen or misplaced, a spare set lets the traveller carry on.
Why does an old toy matter to a child even if it is broken?
The toy carries memories and comfort. Because it has been with the child through many days, it feels like a friend, and losing it feels like losing something personal.
Why does a sieve separate flour from small stones?
The holes let tiny grains pass but hold large bits back. Because the stones are bigger than the openings, they stay on top while the flour falls through.
Why does steel wool glow and burn when lit but a steel rod does not?
The fine strands have a lot of surface for the air. Because oxygen can reach each thin thread easily, it burns while a thick rod loses its heat to the rest of the metal.
Why do windmills turn when the breeze blows?
The wind pushes against the blades. Because the blades are slanted, the moving air makes them spin around the axle.
Why do rivers usually bend and curve instead of running straight?

Rivers wear away the outer bank and drop soil on the inner bank, so they wind. Because the fast water on the outer edge cuts the bank and the slow water on the inner edge leaves silt, each curve grows sharper over time.
Why do scientists repeat an experiment several times before trusting the result?
A repeat checks that the result was not a chance event. Because mistakes and luck can affect any attempt, the same outcome again and again gives confidence.
Why do pickles keep for months in a jar when fresh vegetables spoil in days?
The salt, oil and sourness protect the vegetables. Because these make it hard for germs to grow, the pickle stays good as long as the jar is sealed and kept clean.
Why should we begin a long project well before the deadline?
Starting early leaves room for surprises. Because problems like illness or a missing material can appear without warning, spare days let us fix them without panic.
Why do moths circle around a lamp at night?
Moths seem to be confused by the light. Because they normally use a far-off light such as the moon to fly straight, a close lamp is thought to make them keep turning toward it and spiral around.
Why does a torch with weak batteries give a dim yellowish light?
The weak cells push less current through the bulb. Because the filament stays cooler, it glows less brightly and looks yellower.
Why does a person who feels left out sometimes act rude?
Hurt feelings can come out as anger. Because it is easier to push people away than to admit that we want to be included, the rude behaviour hides the sadness.
Why does a noisy neighbour at night bother us even when the sound is not very loud?
Sleep is easily broken by sounds that we cannot predict. Because the brain stays alert to sudden or repeated noises, even a mild thump can pull us out of rest.
Anita says her brother is older than her. Her brother says Anita is older than him. Can these statements be true together?
No, they cannot be right together. Because each statement rules out the other, the older sibling cannot also be the younger.
Why does a zip close when the slider is pulled up?
The slider forces the teeth together. Because its narrow channel squeezes the rows into a tight interlock, they hold each other until the slider is pulled back.
Why does a shared meal often bring a family closer?
Eating together gives everyone a regular time to talk. Because the family sits face to face with no rush and no screen, small news and jokes are shared and the bond is renewed.
If the bell rings, school is over. The bell is ringing now. Is school over?
Yes, school is over. Because the rule says the bell ringing marks the end of school, the ringing bell tells us that the day has ended.
Why does leather become hard and crack if it is left unused for a long time?
It loses its natural oils. Because the fibres dry out when not treated or flexed, they become stiff and break.
Why is a voice deeper in a person with a larger, longer set of vocal cords?
The longer cords vibrate more slowly. Because slower vibrations make lower notes, long, thick cords give a deeper sound, just as a thick guitar string does.
Why do libraries ask readers to return books on time?
Other readers may be waiting. Because a book can be read by only one reader at a time, a late return keeps another person from enjoying it.
Why is it harder to read in dim light than in bright light?
Dim light makes the eyes work harder. Because less light reaches the page and the pupils must widen to catch it, the letters look less sharp and the eyes tire sooner.
Why does a football bounce less when the air has leaked out of it?
The air gives the ball its spring. Because a ball with less air pushes back less strongly when it hits the ground, it loses its bounce.
Why do trains take a long time to stop?
Trains are heavy and the wheels grip little on steel rails. Because so much weight keeps moving forward and the brakes act on smooth metal, the train needs a long distance to slow down.
Why is it sensible to test a new recipe before cooking for guests?
A trial run shows what might go wrong. Because we find out about taste, timing and missing steps before it matters, the guests get a dish that has been proven to work.
Why does a puddle disappear on a sunny day even though nobody sweeps it away?
The water changes into vapour and rises into the air. Because the sun warms it and the wind carries off the vapour, the puddle slowly dries up.
Why do roots grow downward even when a seed is planted upside down?
The root turns down in response to gravity. Because special cells in the root tip sense which way is down, the root bends and grows that way and the shoot turns up.
Why do white clothes keep us cooler in the sun than black clothes?
White cloth gives back more of the sunlight. Because dark cloth soaks up more light and turns it into heat, a person in black feels warmer under the same sun.
Why do roosters crow in the early morning?
Their body clock tells them dawn is near. Because they respond to light and an inner rhythm, they crow as the sky begins to brighten.
Why does sprinkling salt on cut brinjal draw out water?
The salt pulls water out of the cells. Because water moves toward the stronger salty side, droplets collect on the surface of the slices.
Why does a compass needle keep pointing north?
The needle is a small magnet that lines up with the earth's magnetic field. Because the earth acts like a huge magnet, the free-swinging needle turns until it points along the field toward the north.
Why do some people feel better after cleaning and tidying their room when they are upset?
Tidying gives a feeling of control. Because the mess outside is something they can fix, the work turns the restless energy into something useful and calming.
Why does taking turns on a swing keep a playground calm?
Turns give everyone a fair share. Because each child knows their chance will come, there is less pushing and arguing over who gets to go next.
All the mangoes in the basket are ripe, and this fruit came from the basket. Is it a ripe mango?
This fruit might not be a mango. Because the premises say that every mango in the basket is ripe, they do not say that every fruit in the basket is a mango, so it could be an apple.
Why does iron develop rust when it stays damp for a long time?
Rust forms when iron reacts with water and air. Because the moisture and oxygen slowly change the surface into a crumbly reddish layer, the metal weakens unless it is painted or oiled.
Why do spectacles fog up when we step from an air-conditioned room into the heat?
The cold lenses chill the warm outside air. Because the water vapour in that air cools on the glass and turns to tiny drops, the lenses mist over until they warm up.
Why do shopkeepers greet every customer who walks in?
A greeting makes the customer feel welcome. Because people return to places where they are treated kindly, a friendly hello can bring regular customers.
Why do town councils plant trees along main roads?
Trees give shade and clean the air. Because the leaves cool the pavement and catch dust, walkers and drivers find the road more pleasant.
Why do umpires and referees use whistles instead of shouting?
A whistle carries farther and cuts through noise. Because its sharp high note is different from crowd sounds, players can hear it clearly across a big field.
Why does tea taste bitter if the leaves are left in the water for too long?
More bitter substances come out of the leaves. Because they dissolve slowly into the hot water as time passes, a long steep gives a stronger and harsher taste.
Why do pupils remember a lesson better when they explain it to a friend?
Explaining forces us to organise the ideas. Because we notice the gaps in our own understanding as we speak, we fill them and the lesson sticks.
Why do mango trees drop old flowers without making fruit on every branch?
Only the flowers that get pollinated can grow into fruit. Because many blossoms are never reached by insects or the wind, those flowers wither and fall.
Why do people shout across a valley and hear their own voice return?
The sound hits a distant hillside and bounces back. Because sound reflects from hard, wide surfaces, it returns after a short delay as an echo.
Why do pebbles on a beach look smooth and round?
The waves keep rolling the stones against each other. Because their rough edges wear away when they rub together year after year, the pebbles become smooth.
Why do passengers feel pushed back in their seats when a bus speeds up quickly?
The body wants to keep its place. Because the seat moves forward but the person tends to stay where they were, they feel pressed against the seat back.
Why do we look upside down in the hollow of a spoon but upright on its back?
A curved shiny surface bends the reflection. Because the inside of a spoon curves inward, it flips the picture, while the back curves outward and shows us upright but small.
Why do builders let concrete set for days before putting weight on it?
Concrete needs time to harden. Because the chemical reaction inside it works slowly, loading it too early could crack or weaken it.
Why do honeybees dance inside the hive?
The dance tells other bees where flowers are. Because the angle and length of the movement show the direction and distance of food, the hive members know where to fly.
Why does a sharp smell fill the house when someone fries chillies?
Tiny bits of the chilli oil rise with the hot air. Because they are carried through the room and breathed in, they irritate the nose and throat and make people cough.
Why do some bicycle tyres have patterns on them?

The grooves help the tyre grip loose or muddy ground. Because the raised blocks dig into mud and gravel and the grooves give water and dirt somewhere to go, the tyre slips less off the smooth road. A smooth tyre can still grip well on dry tarmac.
Why does a quiet walk often clear a cluttered mind?
Walking gives the mind some space. Because the steady movement and the changing scenery take attention off our worries, our thoughts settle and we can think more clearly.
A farmer finds that on days when the cock crows, the sun rises soon after. Does the crowing make the sun rise?
No, the crowing does not make the sun rise. Because the cock crows only as dawn is coming, the sun and the crowing share a cause and one does not cause the other.
Why do people in a queue get annoyed when somebody walks to the front?
The person is taking a place that others waited for. Because everybody agreed silently to wait their turn, jumping ahead breaks that fairness and makes the others feel cheated.
Why does cotton cloth feel cooler to wear in summer than polyester cloth?

Cotton usually feels cooler: it lets air through and takes up sweat. Because the loose weave lets air and moisture pass and the absorbed sweat can evaporate from the cloth, heat leaves the skin more easily. Some polyester sports cloth is made to do this too.
Why is a cooking pot with a thick base better for slow simmering?
A thick base spreads heat evenly. Because the heat is not concentrated in a small spot, the food at the bottom is less likely to burn.
Why do eyes blink even when we are not thinking about it?
Blinking keeps the eyes moist and clean. Because each blink spreads a thin layer of tears over the surface and sweeps away dust, the eyes stay comfortable and clear.
Why do readers often find a story more exciting when the hero faces a real danger?
Danger creates suspense. Because the reader wants to know whether the hero will succeed, every page makes them keep reading to see what happens.
Why do neighbours take turns cleaning a shared stairway?
Sharing the job is fair. Because each household uses the stairs, a rota stops a family from doing all the work and keeps the place tidy.
Why do players change ends in some games between halves?
Conditions can favour a team. Because the wind, the sun or the slope of the ground may help a team, switching ends makes the game fair.
Why does a houseplant lean toward the window?
The plant grows toward the light. Because the side of the stem in the shade grows faster than the lit side, the stem bends toward the brighter side.
Why do deserts get hot by day but cold at night?
The dry air holds little moisture to keep the heat. Because there are few clouds or humidity to hold the warmth, the heat escapes quickly after sunset.
Why do aircraft windows have a tiny hole in them?
The hole lets cabin air reach the gap between the panes. Because the pressure there then matches the cabin, the outer pane takes most of the strain and the inner pane is not loaded.
Why do drivers of buses check the tyres and mirrors before starting a journey?
Checking finds faults early. Because a worn tyre or a loose mirror is easy to fix before the trip but dangerous on the road, the check protects the passengers.
Why can a magnifying glass burn a dry leaf in strong sunshine?
The glass gathers the sunlight onto a tiny spot. Because its curved shape bends the rays toward a point, all that light and heat lands in a small place, and the leaf there grows hot enough to scorch.
Why do farmers choose seeds to match the season?
Seeds need the right weather to grow. Because a crop planted in the wrong season may face cold, drought or flood, matching it to the season gives it the best chance.
Why does a whistle make a high note when we blow it hard?
The air inside shakes faster. Because a stronger breath makes the air in the tiny chamber vibrate more quickly, the vibrations reach the ear as a higher pitch.
Why does a teacher repeat a difficult word slowly while writing it on the board?
Slow repetition helps pupils hear and see it together. Because the ear and the eye take it in, the word is easier to remember and spell.
Why are green mangoes sour and ripe mangoes sweet?
Ripening turns acids and starch into sugars. Because the fruit changes its chemicals as it matures on the tree or in the store, the sourness fades and the sweetness grows.
Why does a metal spoon left in a hot cup of tea become hot at the handle?
Heat travels along the metal. Because metal passes heat along its length very well, the warmth from the tea moves up the spoon to the part held in the hand.
Why do cats usually land on their feet when they fall from a low height?
Cats twist their bodies in the air. Because they have very flexible spines and an inner ear that senses which way is down, they turn so the paws meet the ground before the body.
Why does a familiar song bring back old memories so strongly?
The tune is tied to the time we met it. Because the brain stores feelings together with sounds, hearing the melody again can bring back the mood and the scenes from that time.
The path is wet. Does that prove that it rained?
No, it does not prove it. Because a wet path can come from a pipe, a sprinkler or somebody washing the ground, rain is only a possible cause.
Why does a paper aeroplane glide farther when its wings are flat and its nose is pointed?
A pointed nose and flat wings cut through the air with little drag. Because the air slides smoothly past the folds and the wings give lift, the plane stays up longer.
Why do glass windows crack when a hot cup is placed on a very cold sill?
Glass can crack when a part heats up faster than the rest. Because the hot part expands while the cold part does not, the strain inside the glass becomes too great.
Why does a bridge made of arches carry heavy trucks safely?
An arch spreads the load. Because the curve turns the weight into a push along the stones to the supports at the ends, no part carries too much.
Why might a person agree with everything a group says even when they doubt it?
They do not want to stand out. Because disagreeing feels risky in front of others, they stay silent and go along with the group's view.
Why do many stories begin with a problem for the main character to solve?
A problem gives the story a direction. Because readers follow the character's efforts to fix it, the plot has a reason to move forward.
Why do people tap their feet when they hear a lively tune?
The beat invites movement. Because the brain picks up the steady pulse and links it with the body, the foot follows without being told.
Why do villages often build a well or a pond near the middle of the settlement?
A central source is easy for everyone to reach. Because no family has to walk very far, the people share the water and keep an eye on its care.
Why do runners lean forward when starting a sprint?
Leaning helps them push off the ground. Because the body tilts in the direction of the run, the legs can push backward and send the runner forward quickly.
Why does a scab form on a scraped knee?
The blood thickens and dries to cover the wound. Because the dried layer shields the damaged skin from dirt and germs, the body can rebuild new skin below it.
Why does a sunflower seem to follow the sun across the sky?
A young sunflower turns toward the light as it grows. Because the stem grows more on the shaded side, the head tilts toward the bright side as the sun moves.
Why do potters keep their hands wet while shaping clay on a wheel?
Water keeps the clay slippery. Because wet clay lets the hands slide over the spinning surface instead of grabbing and tearing it, the potter can pull the shape up smoothly.
Why does the sky look dark at night even though the stars are shining?
Stars are very far away. Because their light is faint by the time it reaches us and the sun is no longer lighting the air, we see only tiny dots against the dark.
Why is rangoli made on the ground at the entrance of a house?
The doorway is where guests arrive. Because a decorated entrance greets visitors and marks the home as ready for a celebration, the pattern is placed where everyone passes.
Why does a room with no furniture sound echoey?
Sound bounces around the bare room. Because hard walls and floors send the sound back instead of soaking it up, the reflections reach our ears a little after the original voice.
Why do we not feel the earth spinning?
Everything around us moves along with the Earth at a steady pace. Because the spin does not speed up or slow down suddenly, our bodies sense no push, much as a passenger in a smooth train feels none.
Why do volcano slopes often have rich soil that farmers like?
Volcanic ash contains minerals that plants need. Because the ash breaks down slowly and adds nutrients to the ground, crops grow well there.
Why does lemon juice stop cut apples from browning?
The juice slows the colour change. Because its acid and vitamin C interfere with the reaction that turns the flesh brown, the slices stay pale longer.
Why is it wise to charge a phone before a long journey?
A charged phone will not run out when needed. Because a journey may bring delays and we may need maps or calls, a full battery avoids being stranded.
Why does a nonstick pan need a plastic or wooden spoon?
Metal can scratch the coating. Because the thin layer is soft compared with steel, a hard spoon scrapes it off and food starts to stick.
Why does reading aloud help a child learn new words?
Reading aloud uses the eyes, the mouth and the ears together. Because the child sees the word, says it and hears it, the memory forms in many ways.
How does a spider catch insects without chasing them?

Many spiders let a web do the catching. Because the threads are thin, sticky and hard for a flying insect to see, a bug that blunders into them gets stuck, and the spider feels the shaking and walks over.
Why does a boat rock more in the open sea than in a harbour?
The harbour is sheltered from the waves. Because walls and land break up the water movement, a boat tied inside rocks gently while the open sea sends in large swells.
Why does being told the truth gently feel kinder than being told bluntly?
Gentle words show care. Because the same fact can be said in a way that leaves the listener's dignity intact, kindness makes it easier to listen and accept.
Karan always has rice whenever dal is cooked at home. Today he had no rice. Was dal cooked today?
No, dal was not cooked today. Because he has rice every time dal is cooked, a day without rice means the condition for his habit was not met.
Why does a parachute slow a person who is falling?
The parachute catches a lot of air. Because the wide cloth pushes against the air as it drops, the air pushes back strongly and the fall becomes slow.
Why does ink spread on tissue paper but not on glossy paper?
Tissue paper soaks up liquid. Because its loose fibres have tiny gaps that draw in the ink, the ink spreads, whereas glossy paper has a smooth coating that keeps it on the surface.
Why do stairs often have a rail on the side?
The rail gives support if someone slips. Because a hand can grip it to steady the body, people avoid falling, especially children and older people.
Why does an unkind joke hurt even if the joker says it was only fun?
The target feels laughed at. Because the words touch something the person is sensitive about, the joker's intention matters less than the pain that comes from the remark.
Why do cricketers rub the ball on their trousers?
Rubbing keeps a side of the ball smooth and shiny. Because the smooth side moves differently through the air from the rough side, the bowler can make the ball swing.
Why should we keep sharp scissors with their points down when carrying them?
Pointing them down prevents injury if we trip. Because the tips are the dangerous part, holding them toward the floor keeps them away from other people and ourselves.
Why do authors use short sentences when an action scene speeds up?
Short sentences read quickly. Because the rapid rhythm matches the speed of events, the reader feels the pace and the tension.
Why does frost form on grass but not on the pavement beside it?
Grass loses heat more quickly. Because its thin blades cool faster than the ground beneath them on a clear night, they reach freezing sooner and ice collects on them.
Why do people light oil lamps on a windowsill during Diwali rather than only inside the house?
Lamps in the window show the glow to everyone outside. Because light placed at the edge of the home can be seen from the street, it welcomes visitors and shares the festival mood with the neighbours.
Why do the days feel longer in summer and shorter in winter?
The sun stays in the sky for longer in summer. Because the earth is tilted as it goes around the sun, each part leans toward the sun in some months and away in others.
Why does a choir sound fuller than a lone singer?
Many voices add together. Because each singer's sound is slightly different and they blend, the result is richer and louder than a lone voice.
Why does a guitar sound louder with its wooden body than a string stretched alone?

The wooden body takes up the string's shaking and passes it to the air. Because the box vibrates along with the string and moves much more air than a thin string could, the note is louder and carries farther.
Why do sand dunes slowly move across the desert?
The wind carries sand grains up the gentle side. Because the grains tumble down the steep far side and settle there, the whole dune creeps forward.
Why do tailors measure carefully before cutting cloth?
Cloth cannot be put back together after it is cut. Because a wrong cut wastes material and gives a poor fit, careful measuring saves effort and cloth.
Why does milk boil over when we forget it on the stove?
A skin on top of the milk traps the steam and foam. Because the skin holds in the vapour rising from below, the bubbles push the whole layer up and over the rim.
Why do shopkeepers keep fresh stock behind older stock on shelves?
Older goods should be sold before newer ones. Because the newer items would last longer anyway, putting the old ones in front reduces waste from spoilage.
Why does a periscope let a person see over a wall?
The mirrors turn the light around corners. Because a mirror at the top sends the light down the tube and another sends it into the eye, we can look over the obstacle.
Why do our fingers wrinkle when we stay in water for long?
The skin on fingers swells and wrinkles. Because the outer skin layer soaks up water and nerves tighten the blood vessels underneath, the surface gets ridges that may help us grip wet things.
Why do people put dustbins at street corners?
Bins give a handy place for rubbish. Because people are less likely to throw waste on the road when a bin is close, streets stay cleaner.
Why do train wheels have a flange on the inside edge?
The flange keeps the wheel on the rail. Because it presses against the side of the track when the train begins to drift, the wheel is guided back into place.
Why do children sometimes get cranky when they are hungry or sleepy?
A tired or hungry body has less patience. Because the brain depends on rest and fuel to manage feelings, small annoyances turn into big upsets.
Why does a hammer drive a nail into wood more easily than a push with the hand?
The hammer delivers a sudden strong force. Because its weight moves fast and stops on the nail head, all that energy goes into the small area of the nail.
Rohan is in the school choir. Everybody in the choir can sing. Can Rohan sing?
Yes, Rohan can sing. Because he is in the choir and every member can sing, the fact applies to him.
Why can birds sit on a power line without getting hurt?

A bird on one wire has no easy path for current through its body. Because it touches only the wire, there is no difference in electric push between its feet, so the electricity keeps flowing along the wire.
Why does dosa batter swell and smell sour after resting overnight?
The batter ferments. Because tiny organisms in it feed on sugars and make gas and acid, the batter rises and takes on a tangy smell.
Why do we put a date on the pages of a notebook?
The date helps us find things later. Because it records when the work was done, we can look up a lesson or see how our writing has improved.
Why does a plastic bottle left in a hot car sometimes change its shape?
The plastic softens when it gets hot. Because the warm air inside pushes outward on the softened walls, the bottle can bulge, and it may stay warped or sag after it cools.
Why do some flowers close up at night?

Many flowers close to protect their delicate parts. Because shutting the petals helps keep the pollen and the inner parts shielded from cold and damp, the flower is ready to open again when pollinators return in the daylight.
Why does a dripping tap sometimes keep us awake?
The repeated drops make a regular sound. Because the brain keeps listening for the next drip, we cannot ignore it and settle into sleep.
Why does a thank-you note make a helper more likely to help again?
The note shows the helper that the effort was noticed. Because people like to feel that their work matters, they are more willing to give their time again.
Why does reading before bed often help people feel sleepy?
Reading is a calm activity. Because it turns the mind away from daily worries and the eyes get tired, the body slides toward rest.
Why do sweets for a festival often get made days in advance?
Many sweets keep well and need time. Because the cooks can spread the work over many days, nobody is rushed on the day of the festival and the sweets can set properly.
Why do we feel a cool breeze just before rain begins?
Cold air sinks from the storm cloud and spreads out. Because that cool air rushes outward along the ground ahead of the rain, we feel a sudden breeze before the rain arrives.
Why does a conch shell sound like the sea when we hold it to our ear?
We are hearing the noise of the room. Because the hollow shell makes some sounds louder through resonance, the surrounding murmur turns into a soft rushing that resembles waves.
Why do cyclists wear helmets even on quiet roads?
A helmet protects the head in a fall. Because falls can happen anywhere from loose gravel or a pothole, the helmet softens the knock to the skull.
Why do we see colours in a thin layer of oil floating on water?
The oil layer splits the light. Because the light bounces off the top and the bottom of the thin film and the waves combine, some colours get brighter and others fade.
Why do swimmers wear tight caps and suits in a race?
Tight gear reduces drag. Because loose cloth or long hair would catch the water and slow the swimmer, snug clothes let the body glide.
Why does mud crack into patterns as it dries in the sun?
The mud shrinks as it dries. Because the water leaves it and the soil pulls closer together, the surface cannot stretch to cover the same area and it splits.
Why do fire stations keep their trucks ready with the engines facing the road?
A quick start saves time. Because the crew can leave right away without having to turn the vehicle around, they reach the fire sooner.
Why does honey sometimes turn grainy in the jar after many weeks?
The honey is forming sugar crystals. Because it holds more sugar than the water in it can keep dissolved, some sugar slowly settles out as small crystals.
Why does a funnel help us pour liquid into a bottle with a narrow neck?
A funnel catches the pour and leads it into the narrow neck. Because its wide top collects the stream and the narrow end fits the neck, little is spilled.
Why do we yawn when we are tired or bored?
Nobody knows the exact reason, but a common idea is that yawning helps keep us alert. Because a deep yawn draws in a lot of air and stretches the face, it may wake the body up a little.
Why does a tabla player tap the drum with different fingers to change the sound?
Different touches make the skin vibrate differently. Because a stroke in the centre or at the rim changes how the head moves, the tone changes with the place and the finger.
Why does a stream carry leaves away but not heavy rocks?
The water pushes light things more easily. Because a leaf weighs little and the current can lift it, a heavy rock stays on the bed unless the flood is very strong.
Why do postal workers sort letters by area before delivery?
Sorting groups letters on the same route. Because the carrier can then walk or ride in order without crossing the town again and again, deliveries become faster.
Why is salt thrown on icy roads in cold countries?

Salt makes the ice melt at a lower temperature. Because salt dissolves in the thin film of water on the ice, the mixture needs more cold to freeze, so the ice turns to water and the road becomes less slippery.
Why does cut coconut taste flat or off if it is left out for days?
Air and germs slowly spoil the exposed flesh of cut coconut. Because the exposed flesh dries, its oils react with the air and germs begin to grow, the taste turns flat and then unpleasant.
Why do we feel braver after taking a small step towards something scary?
A small step proves that the fear can be faced. Because the worst thing we imagined did not happen, our confidence grows and the next step looks easier.
Why do bats hang upside down when they rest?

Hanging upside down is a handy way for bats to rest and take off. Because their legs are weak for standing, they can simply drop from the perch into flight and keep out of reach of many animals on the ground.
Why do hill roads wind in curves instead of going straight up?
Curves make the slope gentler. Because a straight road would be too steep for vehicles to climb or brake safely, the road zigzags to spread the climb over a longer distance.
Why does a map help us understand a story set in a faraway land?
The map shows where events happen. Because we can picture the distances and the places in the tale, the story feels more real and easier to follow.
Why do gardeners plant tall crops on the side where they will not shade the short ones?
Tall plants block sunlight. Because short plants need light to grow well, placing tall ones on the far side lets everything receive its share.
Why does a lock open only with its own key?
The key's cuts match the pins inside. Because each cut lifts a pin to the exact height needed, the lock turns only when the shape fits.
Why do flowers often have bright petals and a sweet smell?
The colour and scent attract insects. Because bees and butterflies come looking for nectar and carry pollen from flower to flower, the plant is able to make seeds.
Why do aluminium foil sheets crinkle and hold their shape?
The thin metal is easy to bend and stays bent. Because the metal does not spring back like paper, a fold or a crumple remains where it was made.
The lamp works only if the plug is in the socket. The plug is in the socket. Will the lamp work?
Not necessarily. Because the plug in the socket is needed but may not be enough, the bulb could be fused or the switch could be off.
Why do shy people sometimes find it easier to talk in a small group than in a large hall?
A small group feels safer. Because fewer people are watching and each person can see everyone's reaction, the worry about being judged is smaller.
